Study companion · Ishvara Yoga 145 videos → 219 teachings · Anatoly Zenchenko

The body is the instrument.
The goal is a state.

Everything Anatoly teaches across 145 lessons rests on a few refusals: don't stretch, don't force a joint open, don't fight your body. Move by balance and contraction, earn the nervous system's trust — and the shape arrives on its own.

↓ read the teachings

00

One thread through all of it

Watch the videos in sequence and one idea keeps returning across every topic: the body is not to be forced, but understood. No instruction is about reaching further. Every one is about moving so that the nervous system permits the movement.

Don't stretch. Don't "open." Balance — and the body stops defending itself opens on its own.

The 219 teachings below decode Anatoly's channel: first principles and the logic of the body, then the method of practice, breath and the locks, and a library of specific technique for each asana. Switch languages with the toggle at top right.

01

First principles

Before any pose, a handful of refusals — the ground everything stands on: yoga is for you, not the reverse; the body is the instrument, the state is the goal.

Philosophy

Yoga is for you — you are not for yoga. Stop working through pain and self-coercion. Your practice should give you energy and curiosity; you should look for opportunities to practice, not force yourself onto the mat.

why · mistakehide

Why A practice built on self-force is a war with yourself, and whoever wins, you lose. When practice becomes accessible and interesting, it sustains itself.

Common mistake Pushing through pain, believing suffering equals progress.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 3

Philosophy

Yoga is gymnastics for the brain and nervous system. The body is the instrument, not the goal. In every asana the goal is a state — to feel good in the position, not merely to achieve a shape.

why · mistakehide

Why Ha and Tha represent consciousness and subconscious. Yoga integrates them; every asana, breath, and purification is a means toward that integration.

Common mistake Treating the achievement of a shape as the goal rather than inner wellbeing inside it.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 3 · Анатолий Зенченко. Основные техники йоги

Philosophy

There are no strength asanas in yoga. Every posture people call a strength asana is actually a balance asana. Align the center of gravity with the support points and what seemed to require force becomes effortless.

why · mistakehide

Why With correct alignment you can hold 'difficult' postures indefinitely; force is only needed when alignment is wrong.

Common mistake Muscling through postures rather than finding the balance point.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. В йоге нет силовых асан · Анатолий Зенченко о семинаре "Биомеханика асан"

Philosophy

Asana means a comfortable and stable position of the body in space (sukham, sthiram). There is nothing in this definition about suffering, overstretching, or overcoming resistance — if a position is uncomfortable, it is not an asana.

why · mistakehide

Why Any position that is natural for the body from the standpoint of anatomy and physiology is already achievable with normal human mobility — no unusual bone structure or superhuman flexibility is required.

Common mistake Treating pain or severe discomfort as a necessary part of practice, or pushing through suffering as if it proves you are 'doing yoga.'

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 1

Philosophy

Expand your comfort zone from within — do not leap outside it. The goal is to make the zone of comfort as large as possible while remaining inside it. Beyond its boundary lies uncontrolled, dangerous territory.

why · mistakehide

Why Forced practice beyond the comfort zone triggers protective reflexes that actually reduce coordination and mobility. Steady expansion from within builds genuine, lasting change without injury.

Common mistake Following the popular cliché 'leave your comfort zone' in physical practice — forcing postures beyond current capacity prevents the neural learning that would allow real progress.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 1

Philosophy

In an asana, what you need is not the form but the state — the feeling of being well in that position. When you have found that state, you are done; move to the next challenge.

why · mistakehide

Why The body shape is a byproduct; the real training is learning to be coherent and at ease in an uncomfortable situation — a skill that transfers directly to life.

Common mistake Chasing the external shape of the pose at the expense of inner coherence.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Йога, как способ достижения целей в жизни · Ішвара йога. Анатолій Зенченко. Основи йоги. Питання для початківця

Philosophy

The nervous system reacts to the loudest signals. Symptoms shout; the cause is silent, in the area you do not feel. Train your attention to go toward areas of no sensation — that is where the real cause lives.

why · mistakehide

Why Non-working muscle groups produce no proprioceptive signal — you cannot feel them, which is why they remain unaddressed and continue to cause problems elsewhere.

Common mistake Always stretching or treating where it hurts, instead of investigating where nothing is felt.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Йога, как способ достижения целей в жизни

Philosophy

Yoga is the difference between the 'strong' way and the 'smart' way. The strong way: where it pulls, I stretch it more to defeat it. The smart way: assess what is not at ease, find how to remove it, feel yourself deeply, and arrive at wholeness.

why · mistakehide

Why Force applied to the wrong place deepens the problem; intelligent investigation of sensation leads to real resolution.

Common mistake Declaring the body the enemy and trying to 'defeat' it through stretching.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Йога, как способ достижения целей в жизни

Philosophy

Yoga teaches you to breathe evenly, even to smile, in very difficult positions and situations. This is the actual training — learning to be comfortable in any difficult circumstance of life.

why · mistakehide

Why The mat serves as a controlled laboratory for practicing equanimity under physical stress.

Source Ішвара йога. Анатолій Зенченко. Основи йоги. Питання для початківця

Philosophy

Yoga is 99% practice and 1% theory. Real change comes from regularly — at least three times per week over years — spending time on the mat turning toward yourself and learning to feel what is happening inside.

why · mistakehide

Why Inner change accretes slowly through consistent self-directed attention; no amount of theory can substitute for direct repeated experience.

Common mistake Attending workshops sporadically and expecting transformation without near-daily practice.

Source Как йога меняет жизнь. Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар выходного дня в Киеве. · Ішвара йога. Анатолій Зенченко. Основи йоги. Питання для початківця

Philosophy

There are two kinds of practitioners: 'strong' ones stretch whatever is tight and push through whatever hurts; 'smart' ones recognize that tightness and pain are symptoms, find the root cause, and eliminate it. Always be the smart one.

why · mistakehide

Why Pain and restriction are effects of a deeper misalignment — usually an inactive muscle or a mispositioned pelvis. Stretching the symptom does not correct the cause and often causes injury.

Common mistake Treating the tight or painful structure (hamstrings, hip, lower back) as the problem and forcing it to change directly.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О сильных и умных людях

Philosophy

Your body is always on your side. When you feel resistance or tightness, the body is not your enemy — it is protecting you. Do not fight the resistance; give the body the correct movement signal and the resistance will disappear.

why · mistakehide

Why The body activates stabilizer muscles (e.g., hamstrings) when it detects a loss of balance or an unfamiliar movement — because you have not signaled your intention through the correct muscles. Once the correct muscles engage, the protective reflex releases.

Common mistake Interpreting muscular resistance as stubbornness or weakness that must be overcome with more force.

Source Монолог о теле. Анатолий Зенченко. · О задней поверхности бедра. Анатолий Зенченко.

Philosophy

You experience your body as something separate from 'you' — as an external object you pull and push around. Stop managing the body from outside with your hands and arms. Learn to initiate movement from the inside, through the muscles that are responsible for that movement.

why · mistakehide

Why The subconscious/body only recognizes genuine movement signals through the correct muscles. External pulling triggers protective stabilization rather than the intended movement.

Common mistake Using hands or arms to pull yourself into a forward fold, twist, or any other pose — this is not movement, it is dragging an object.

Source Монолог о теле. Анатолий Зенченко.

Philosophy

Yoga's primary goal is to develop the brain's ability to control the body. Flexibility, health, and freedom from pain are valuable side effects — not the goal. The practice deliberately places the brain in strange, unfamiliar positions and forces it to figure out how to keep the body integrated and safe. That is the actual training.

why · mistakehide

Why The body is not the problem. The only real problem in yoga is the brain's inability to properly coordinate and control the body as an instrument. Everything else — tightness, weakness, poor balance — is a downstream consequence of this fundamental disconnect.

Common mistake Treating yoga as physical stretching and chasing asana forms as an end goal misses the entire point and commonly results in injury because the body is forced into shapes without the brain having developed the control to manage them safely.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Как работает йога или как устранить проблемы в практике mp4

Philosophy

The body will only give you its natural range of motion when it is convinced you are not going to harm it. You must create internal wholeness — the felt sense that the owner is fully in charge — before the body will cooperate in difficult positions. You can only convince the body through demonstrated care, not through force.

why · mistakehide

Why The body's protective intelligence operates subconsciously. It tightens and restricts range of motion as an automatic safety mechanism whenever it senses uncontrolled or threatening movement.

Common mistake Forcing the body through pain does not convince it of your good intentions — it deepens the distrust and causes the body to protect itself even more aggressively on subsequent attempts.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Как работает йога или как устранить проблемы в практике mp4

Philosophy

Most claimed physiological limitations in yoga — 'shortened Achilles tendons,' 'restricted hip anatomy' — are not real structural limitations but simply the result of not activating the correct muscles. A genuine structural limitation requires documented medical diagnosis with imaging. Without that evidence, treat any limitation as functional and search for the missing muscle activation pattern.

why · mistakehide

Why People who seek excuses vastly outnumber those who seek solutions, and knowledge of physiology has been misused to generate sophisticated-sounding justifications. True structural limits — such as genuinely shortened femoral neck — affect perhaps 2% of the population and require radiological confirmation.

Common mistake Using physiological concepts as ready-made excuses before doing the work of finding the correct movement pattern is self-deception that ensures you stay exactly where you are.

Source О влиянии физиологических особенностей в йоге. Анатолий Зенченко.

Philosophy

Emotional blocks in the body are, at the physical level, a state in which one muscle or group is chronically over-contracted while its antagonist is too weak to balance it. To resolve an emotional block, balance the tone of both sides — do not simply try to relax the tight side.

why · mistakehide

Why Relaxing the over-contracted side alone leaves the body without structural support and the pattern returns immediately.

Common mistake Trying to 'release' or 'breathe away' an emotional block without activating the opposing, dormant muscle group.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Как йога работает с эмоциональными блоками

Philosophy

All yoga techniques are primarily directed at changing the state of consciousness — the body is the instrument for doing this. All health improvements (less pain, more vitality) are positive side effects, not the primary aim. Both purposes are valid; be honest about which one you are pursuing.

why · mistakehide

Source О побочных эффектах йоги. Изменение состояния сознания. Анатолий Зенченко.

Philosophy

An asana is a comfortable and stable position in space — there is nothing in its definition about suffering, forcing, or overcoming. The body is anatomically capable of all asanas. What is missing is not flexibility but the brain's ability to coordinate the right muscle groups correctly.

why · mistakehide

Why Reframing from 'stretch the body' to 'improve neural coordination' changes the practice to something trainable without pain and non-injurious.

Common mistake Thinking inability to do an asana means insufficient flexibility, when in fact it means insufficient nervous-system coordination.

Source Что такое асана? Анатолий Зенченко. · Анатолий Зенченко. О методике Ишвара-йога. 1 часть

Philosophy

Yoga is brain training that uses the body as equipment. Gradually improve three components in parallel — body energy (the battery), nervous-system conductivity (the wire), and brain capacity (the light bulb). Suddenly changing any single component burns out the others; progress must be gradual and balanced across all three.

why · mistakehide

Why Each component depends on the others. Forcing rapid change in one (e.g. extreme body training) without corresponding development of the others overloads and damages the system.

Common mistake Pushing body flexibility hard while neglecting nervous system development and awareness practice, or chasing sudden spiritual experiences before the body and nervous system can handle increased energy.

Source Йога: свобода, осознанность и ответственность. Анатолий Зенченко · Йога - это гимнастика для мозга. Анатолий Зенченко.

Philosophy

Do not try to overpower the subconscious — you will never win. The subconscious will simply shut you down, as when you try to hold your breath by force and eventually faint. The only viable approach is to befriend it: create conditions it finds interesting and enjoyable. If you feel pleasure in practice, it is working correctly.

why · mistakehide

Why Breathing, heartbeat, and most motor patterns are governed by the subconscious. Any conscious attempt to override them triggers a protective shutdown. Cooperation — not domination — is the only mechanism available.

Common mistake Practicing through pain, forcing the breath, or approaching practice as 'defeating yourself' — these declare war on the subconscious, which will always win.

Source Йога: свобода, осознанность и ответственность. Анатолий Зенченко · Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара-йога - йога внутренней целостности

Philosophy

The core principle of Ishvara Yoga is inner wholeness. Before attempting any asana, first establish a state where the body does not feel threatened. When the body senses it will not be 'broken apart,' it releases the protective muscular bracing that practitioners mistake for inflexibility.

why · mistakehide

Why Protective muscular contraction is an automatic response to perceived structural threat. Once the threat signal disappears, those muscles release and natural range of motion becomes available without force.

Common mistake Interpreting protective muscular bracing as 'tight muscles that need stretching' and responding with more force — which only escalates the body's defensive response.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара-йога - йога внутренней целостности

Philosophy

Ishvara Yoga draws joints together and collects the body — it does not open and stretch joints. Most methods try to increase range by opening; we create stability and coordinated movement by compressing and integrating.

why · mistakehide

Why A collected joint is stable, controllable, and capable of transmitting force accurately. An 'opened' joint with overstretched connective tissue loses structural integrity.

Common mistake Assuming that more 'opening' of joints automatically means better yoga or greater health.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. О методике Ишвара-йога. 1 часть · Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О многообразии методик йоги.

Philosophy

In Ayurveda, health means your current dosha balance matches your unique birthright constitution — not that all three doshas are equal at 33/33/33. Whatever your dominant dosha at birth, that ratio IS your norm and the condition for your health. Allow yourself to be who you are, not who you think you should be.

why · mistakehide

Why Trying to suppress a dominant dosha or achieve a theoretical equal balance works against the body's natural design and disrupts health rather than supporting it.

Common mistake Assuming that a dominant dosha (e.g. Vata or Kapha) is a flaw to be corrected, when it is the individual's natural and healthy constitutional template.

Source Анатолий Зенченко о дошах!

Philosophy

All asanas, even the most complex, lie within the natural range of motion of the human body. You need no superhuman flexibility beyond what you already have. If an asana required movement outside the joint's natural range, you could do it only once — with the sound of something breaking.

why · mistakehide

Why The human body is already equipped for every asana in the tradition. The challenge is learning to use what you naturally have.

Common mistake Believing yoga requires forcing the body into unnatural positions, and that pain means you should push harder.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Open Air 2015. Киев. Теория

Philosophy

The purpose of asana practice is to train the brain — to teach it to manage the instrument called the body. Working with the body in yoga develops consciousness; it is not about achieving impressive shapes.

why · mistakehide

Why Asana practice that makes the brain solve genuinely novel coordination problems expands mental capacity.

Common mistake Treating yoga as a flexibility or fitness discipline and measuring progress by depth of a posture rather than quality of control.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Open Air 2015. Киев. Теория · Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О стойке на голове и Йоге с большой буквы "Й".

Philosophy

If an asana feels painful — muscles tearing, ligaments straining, bones grinding — you are not doing yoga. Yoga means being in a natural position of the body in space: it should feel good. Pain means the brain has not yet learned to coordinate the instrument called the body.

why · mistakehide

Why Pain in a position within the body's natural range always signals a coordination failure — the wrong muscles working or the right ones absent — never productive work.

Common mistake Treating pain and burning during stretching as a sign of progress and pushing through it.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Open Air 2015. Киев. Теория

02

The logic of the body

His anatomy is a way of thinking, not a chart to memorize: muscles contract — never stretch; a joint is held by tone, not opened; everything moves in chains.

Anatomy

Abandon the concept of 'stretching muscles.' Every movement is produced by muscle contraction, not stretching. The idea that you lengthen a muscle by pulling on it is physiologically invalid.

why · mistakehide

Why The belly of a muscle is not meaningfully elastic; movement is created by shortening.

Common mistake Forcing passive elongation, overstressing tendons and ligaments while target muscles stay braced.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 3

Anatomy

Never try to 'open' or pull apart a joint. A joint is two bone ends held near each other by muscle tension. Limited mobility means the brain cannot command the surrounding muscles into tone — the joint is not at fault.

why · mistakehide

Why If you could actually 'open' a joint you would destroy it. Bones stay together because muscles crossing the joint are contracted.

Common mistake Treating the joint space as the problem and trying to create space inside it.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 3

Anatomy

Never stretch ligaments. They run bone-to-bone as the last line of defense — holding bones together when muscular control is lost. Once overstretched, they cannot recover.

why · mistakehide

Why Ligament function is emergency stabilization; once overstretched the joint becomes chronically unstable.

Common mistake Forcing extreme end range believing you lengthen the muscle, when you load the ligaments.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 3

Anatomy

The spine and brain are the most important things in yoga. Spinal position determines pelvic position; pelvic position determines leg mobility. If the spine is unstable, the body automatically switches off leg mobility to protect it.

why · mistakehide

Why Swinging a heavy lever (the leg) without a stable spine sends rotation into the lumbar and injures it; the nervous system prevents this by restricting leg range.

Common mistake Chasing leg flexibility while ignoring spinal stabilization.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 3

Anatomy

Muscles operate in chains — one influences the next like links of a tank tread. If one link is hypertonic or hypotonic, the whole chain is disrupted. Your practice is to find the 'stuck' links and restore their natural tone.

why · mistakehide

Why If one link seizes, the whole track jams; the visible problem is often a symptom of a disruption elsewhere in the chain.

Common mistake Treating only the symptomatic location without finding the cause up- or downstream.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 3

Anatomy

The psoas major is not merely a hip flexor. When the leg is fixed, it tilts the spine forward. It is the key deep connector between the body's center and the legs and primarily governs lumbar position.

why · mistakehide

Why Its function reverses depending on which end is fixed; most know only the hip-flexion role and miss its lumbar-stabilizing role.

Common mistake Treating the psoas only as a hip flexor.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 3

Anatomy

Fear leaves a permanent physical imprint. The stress response is universal: tuck the head into the shoulders and close the chest and abdomen. Years of accumulated fear locks this pattern; consistent yoga gradually releases it.

why · mistakehide

Why Accumulated fear is held as chronic tension in the psoas, chest, and throat; new stress reproduces the closure pattern.

Common mistake Treating stiffness as purely physical, ignoring its emotional roots.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 3

Anatomy

The adductors have three functions: (1) bring the leg toward the midline, (2) rotate the femur inward, (3) draw the leg axially into the hip socket. Use all three to organize the hip-pelvis relationship.

why · mistakehide

Why Understanding all three lets you use the adductors to govern rotation and axial engagement of the hip complex, not just squeeze the legs together.

Common mistake Knowing only the adduction function.

Source О приводящих мышцах бёдер. Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар выходного дня в Киеве.

Anatomy

Cultivate healthy background muscle tone — neither too slack nor too tight. A slack muscle is like liquid and cannot transmit a movement wave; an over-contracted muscle is frozen and also cannot. Only the middle state lets the impulse travel through the body.

why · mistakehide

Why Muscle fibers must be aligned and mutually engaged to transmit movement as a traveling wave.

Common mistake Equating complete relaxation with healthy tone, or over-bracing to feel stable.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О том, почему так важен тонус мышц.

Anatomy

The highest concentration of proprioceptors is at the muscle-to-bone attachment sites (entheses), where tendon meets bone. Direct attention to these attachment points to recruit multiple muscle groups at once and develop precise motor control.

why · mistakehide

Why Proprioceptors at attachment points sense joint position and load and feed motor-control loops; attending to them improves coordination far more than attending to the muscle belly.

Common mistake Directing awareness only to the belly of a muscle.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 3

Anatomy

The nervous system fatigues before the muscles do. What becomes exhausted during practice is the brain's ability to send precise commands — not the muscle tissue itself. Work with attention, not with force.

why · mistakehide

Why Familiar neural pathways conduct impulses easily. New or unfamiliar commands require far more nervous system effort — that is why the brain tires when you try to engage the navel or mula bandha. This mental fatigue is a sign the neural wiring is being built, not a sign of weakness.

Common mistake Interpreting mental fatigue or inability to maintain bandhas as muscular weakness — the real limitation is the absence of an established neural pathway, not a lack of physical strength.

Source Тело: ключи к работе с телом в практике асан. Анатолий Зенченко

Anatomy

Every asana is a movement, not a static shape. You move into the position and continue to move within it — even in a held posture, you are actively deepening or maintaining internal motion.

why · mistakehide

Why Static holding without internal movement causes the body to lock up and trigger protective tension. Continuous micro-movement maintains muscle coordination and allows safe deepening.

Common mistake Reaching a 'final position' and stopping all internal effort, treating the pose as a destination rather than an ongoing process.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 1

Anatomy

When you attempt a forward bend by pulling yourself down with your hands, the body's protective reflex activates — it reads it as falling and contracts the hamstrings and spinal extensors to save you. The muscles are not your enemy; they are protecting you.

why · mistakehide

Why The subconscious motor system treats gravity-driven collapse as a threat and contracts the posterior chain to prevent it. To bypass this reflex, you need to actively engage the muscles that tilt the pelvis anteriorly, signaling that the movement is controlled.

Common mistake Pulling yourself into forward bends with the hands — this triggers exactly the protective contraction that stops the movement.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 1 · Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Техники «раскрытия» тазобедренных суставов

Anatomy

Stop thinking about stretching muscles. A muscle is a spring with fixed attachment points and cannot be permanently lengthened. The real task is to identify and activate the correct muscles, which allows the restrictive muscles to release on their own.

why · mistakehide

Why Any attempt to force a muscle beyond its natural range triggers a stretch reflex — a protective contraction. Working with the antagonist activating muscles creates space and mobility without fighting the body's protective mechanisms.

Common mistake Years of forcing or 'pulling' at hamstrings, hip flexors, or back muscles — these muscles contract in response to the very pressure meant to release them.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 1 · Про растягивания и вытягивания. Анатолий Зенченко.

Anatomy

Nature abhors a vacuum. Never try to 'create space' or 'pull vertebrae apart.' Your vertebrae are held together with a force equivalent to a bulldog's jaw — if you could actually stretch them apart, you would disintegrate. If a vacuum forms in a joint, the body fills it with pathology.

why · mistakehide

Why Joint health depends on maintaining appropriate compression with coordinated surrounding muscles. A surgically or forcibly created vacuum inside a joint will be filled with effusion, inflammation, or degeneration.

Common mistake Believing that 'decompression' traction approaches in asana practice are beneficial — any artificially created vacuum will be filled by the body with something unwanted.

Source Про растягивания и вытягивания. Анатолий Зенченко. · Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 1

Anatomy

Two main reasons asanas do not work: (1) lack of bodily wholeness — different parts of the body are not interacting with each other in a given movement; (2) lack of coordinated interaction between antagonist muscle pairs.

why · mistakehide

Why Every movement requires paired muscle groups to work in coordinated opposition. When antagonists are not balanced, one side over-contracts or under-activates, blocking the joint or making the movement dangerous.

Common mistake Targeting one muscle group in isolation (e.g., trying to 'open the hamstrings') while ignoring the antagonist — the real cause of restriction is usually the imbalance of the pair, not a single tight muscle.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Почему не получаются асаны. · Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Как устранить проблемы в практике

Anatomy

The diaphragm is the most powerful internal muscle of the body. Learn to control it — keep it open (expanded downward), not compressed. Controlling the diaphragm gives you control over breathing, the position of the ribcage, and the position of the spine.

why · mistakehide

Why A locked diaphragm collapses the ribcage, compresses the lumbar spine, and makes coordinated breathing impossible. An open diaphragm creates the axial support needed for all deep asana work.

Common mistake Compressing the belly or rounding the lower back to 'engage the core' — this locks the diaphragm and destroys spinal support.

Source Ішвара йога. Анатолій Зенченко. Важність внутрішніх м'язів тіла на прикладі діафрагми · Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар под Киевом · Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Техника выполнения Бхастрики

Anatomy

The diaphragm — not the erector spinae, not the glutes — is the conductor of your spine. It determines the position of the spine in space. The erector only straightens; it cannot arch the back the way you think it does.

why · mistakehide

Why The diaphragm is dome-shaped and attaches from just below the shoulder blades down to L3–L4 along the front of the spine; it works in tandem with the psoas to establish both thoracic lift and lumbar lordosis.

Common mistake Squeezing the glutes or over-contracting back muscles in backbends — this blocks spinal movement and is why your back still hurts after years of practice.

Source Уддияна бандха. Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Anatomy

Any muscle has two phases: first stabilization, then mobilization. Do not over-contract in the stabilization phase — even a correctly engaged muscle held too tightly will prevent the movement you want. Use just enough tone to stabilize, then let the movement happen.

why · mistakehide

Why Excessive stabilization-phase tone prevents the joint from moving at all — for example, an over-gripped neck prevents any head movement.

Common mistake Tightening everything as hard as possible in the name of 'engagement' — this is greed in practice.

Source Уддияна бандха. Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Anatomy

The body has a center — the space just behind the navel. Develop real proprioception of this center by placing four fingers of both hands and pressing gently inward until you actually feel inside your abdominal cavity.

why · mistakehide

Why After about two weeks of daily manual exploration you can navigate your interior, feel lumbar tension, locate hypertonicity, and even count vertebrae from the front.

Common mistake Treating 'pull navel to spine' as a purely verbal instruction without developing the actual sensation.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О центре тела

Anatomy

If you have a problem in the back (a specific spinal level), you can feel it from the front. Pressing into the abdomen opposite that spinal level, you will find a puffiness — muscles in hypertonus. Work gently from the front to improve blood and lymph flow to that area.

why · mistakehide

Why The front and back of each spinal level are functionally linked; the anterior deep muscles accessible through the abdomen mirror the posterior tension.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О центре тела

Anatomy

Among all the body's diaphragms (cranial, thoracic, pelvic floor), the thoracic diaphragm is the most important because it is the largest. When you correctly set the largest structure, all others align around it. Start there.

why · mistakehide

Why It is easier for the largest structure to reorganize smaller ones around it than the reverse.

Source Дафрагма: значение и функции в работе с телом. Анатолий Зенченко

Anatomy

A muscle is a spring with fixed attachment points — it can contract, relax, and extend to its natural length. Any attempt to make it longer than designed destroys its function. A 'stretched' muscle is like a stretched rubber band: it cannot generate force and is non-functional.

why · mistakehide

Why Muscle tissue is not elastic connective tissue. Overstretching disrupts the actin-myosin mechanism and the muscle can no longer produce force efficiently.

Common mistake Believing that holding a 'stretch' in a muscle will create permanent lengthening that improves flexibility.

Source О задней поверхности бедра. Анатолий Зенченко.

Anatomy

The iliopsoas (large lumbar muscles) is the true mover of the torso in forward bends — not the back muscles, not the abs. It connects the rib cage to the legs. If it does not work, your rib cage movement is blocked and you lose sensation in your legs.

why · mistakehide

Why The iliopsoas originates at the iliac crest wings, runs along the spine and attaches to the lesser trochanter of the femur — it literally bridges the torso and the legs and is responsible for anterior pelvic tilt (the fold).

Common mistake Trying to create a forward fold by pulling with the back muscles or 'engaging the core' with abdominal bracing.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О больших поясничных мышцах. · О задней поверхности бедра. Анатолий Зенченко.

Anatomy

The abdominal muscles are NOT antagonists to the back muscles — this is a widespread misconception. The true antagonist pair that controls the spine and pelvis is: iliopsoas (front, tilts pelvis forward) and gluteal muscles (back, tilts pelvis back). Train this pair, not the abs-vs-back model.

why · mistakehide

Why The spine is controlled by deep muscles close to it, not the superficial abdominal wall. Working the wrong antagonist pair leaves the real movers underdeveloped.

Common mistake Doing crunches or abdominal work to 'fix' lower back pain — abs cannot solve lumbar problems because they are not the real antagonists of the lumbar extensors.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О больших поясничных мышцах.

Anatomy

The true 'core' is the diaphragm and iliopsoas — the deep muscles at the center of the body. Abdominals (including the transverse) and glutes are NOT core muscles. You can hold plank positions indefinitely using only the true core, with abs and glutes completely relaxed.

why · mistakehide

Why Core means what determines spine position and movement from the inside — the deep postural muscles. Outer muscles are superficial movers; they exhaust quickly when used for postural stabilization.

Common mistake Thinking planks, crunches, or glute bridges train the core; they train the periphery, not the structural center.

Source Мышцы кора. Анатолий Зенченко.

Anatomy

The diaphragm is the largest muscle in the body — larger than the glutes. In most people it is chronically compressed and stuck in a half-exhale state. Before any practice, consciously open and expand it on the first inhalation, and keep it in that open position throughout.

why · mistakehide

Why A compressed diaphragm blocks both full breathing and free spinal movement. It is the gateway to all the other internal muscles functioning correctly.

Common mistake Beginning pranayama or asana with a compressed diaphragm; not taking a dedicated opening breath before starting.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О больших поясничных мышцах. · Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Техника выполнения Капалабхати

Anatomy

To create integrity in any joint, direct your attention to equally draw the two bones toward each other from all sides simultaneously — a small, equal muscle tone from inside, outside, front, and behind — regardless of whether the joint is straight, bent, or at an angle.

why · mistakehide

Why Equal tension from all sides is like balanced reins — the joint is stable, protected, and responds accurately. Any imbalance in that tension destabilizes the joint and reduces its range of safe motion.

Common mistake Trying to 'open' or deepen joints; asymmetric engagement of joint muscles creates instability rather than freedom.

Source Как создать целостность любого сустава. Анатолий Зенченко.

Anatomy

About 50% of the body's muscles form a chain that connects downward to the ground, absorbing and transferring weight like springs. The other 50% form a chain that extends and lifts the body upward. Balance these two chains along the spine and every other body part — legs, arms, head — will automatically find correct alignment.

why · mistakehide

Why The spine is the central axis to which all internal organs and limbs attach. Balanced muscular tension along it creates the structural condition that everything else depends on.

Common mistake Working individual muscles in isolation rather than engaging both chains as a coordinated whole.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О работе мускулатуры тела.

Anatomy

Quality dietary fats are essential for gas exchange in the lungs — not only as energy. When body fat drops too low, pulmonary gas exchange deteriorates significantly. When quality fats are present in adequate amounts, gas exchange improves. Do not restrict fats in your diet.

why · mistakehide

Why Pulmonary surfactant, which prevents alveolar collapse and regulates gas exchange, is primarily a phospholipid — it depends directly on the quality and availability of dietary fats.

Common mistake Restricting dietary fat intake under the assumption that it benefits yoga practice or physical health.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Зависимость газообмена в легких от наличия жиров

Anatomy

The iliopsoas creates lumbar lordosis by rotating the coccyx backward, shifting the sacrum into its correct position. This natural lumbar curve is not a postural problem to be corrected — it is the correct baseline position of your lower spine.

why · mistakehide

Why The iliopsoas controls the alignment of all five lumbar vertebrae. Its tonic contraction holds the sacrum in the correct forward-tilted position and determines the baseline shape of the entire lumbar region.

Source Подвздошно поясничная мышца. Подробный разбор. Анатолий Зенченко

Anatomy

As the iliopsoas rotates the tailbone backward (nutation), the quadriceps and adductors respond by pushing the iliac wings forward as a counter-movement — this stabilizes the pelvis and keeps you upright. The sacrum and iliac wings are separate structures that move independently; their coordinated opposition is your pelvic balance system.

why · mistakehide

Why This is a system of counterweights: the more the iliopsoas rotates the sacrum back, the more the quadriceps and adductors move the iliac wings forward to compensate. Without this interplay you would simply fall forward.

Common mistake Tucking the tailbone under (counter-nutation) collapses this entire system, progressively disconnects the legs, and destroys the healthy lumbar curve. It is one of the most common destructive instructions given in yoga.

Source Подвздошно поясничная мышца. Подробный разбор. Анатолий Зенченко

Anatomy

The quadriceps will not activate as a pelvic stabilizer unless the spinal erector muscles are working first. Without the spinal muscles creating the iliopsoas-mediated lordosis signal, the quadriceps have nothing to respond to — they remain asleep. The chain always starts from above.

why · mistakehide

Why Stabilization reflexes are sequential: spinal muscles activate iliopsoas, iliopsoas creates the sacral rotation, that rotation is the stimulus for the quadriceps and adductors to engage. Break the chain at the beginning and nothing below fires.

Source Подвздошно поясничная мышца. Подробный разбор. Анатолий Зенченко

Anatomy

Approximately 60% of people have a psoas minor — a small third muscle that attaches to the pubic bone and gives additional refined control over pelvic tilt. If you have it, you have a structural advantage. There is no way to know without MRI or specialized ultrasound — so do not assume either way.

why · mistakehide

Why The psoas minor's attachment to the pubis gives it a mechanical advantage for controlling pelvic tilt that the psoas major alone cannot provide.

Source Корневой замок. Мулабандха. Анатолий Зенченко

Anatomy

When the posterior diaphragm is released and active, the shoulder naturally settles back and down — the arm becomes a true extension of the spinal lever. When the posterior diaphragm is compressed or inactive, the shoulder will automatically rise toward the ear, no matter how hard you try to consciously press the shoulder blade down.

why · mistakehide

Why The musculature that connects the arm to the thorax rides on the tension state of the diaphragm. A free posterior diaphragm creates the correct foundational tension for proper arm-to-spine connection.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Задняя часть диафрагмы.

Anatomy

If the hip joint is not moving the way you want, the root cause is that you cannot stabilize the pelvis. When the pelvis is unstabilized, the subconscious removes your ability to command the leg muscles — the muscles exist, but you cannot access them. Establish pelvic stability first; hip range of motion follows automatically.

why · mistakehide

Why Pelvic control is the prerequisite for all lower limb mobility. The subconscious will not allow the hip joint to operate at full range from an unstable, uncontrolled base.

Source Работа с суставами. Анатолий Зенченко.

Anatomy

The knee joint can flex/extend and, when bent to 90° or more, it can rotate — and the greater the bend, the greater the available rotation angle. This is physiologically normal and is exploited in Virasana and Padmasana. What the knee cannot do in any position is deviate laterally — pushing the shin sideways out of the sagittal plane. That is not 'opening the knee'; it is damaging it.

why · mistakehide

Why The knee's collateral ligaments exist specifically to prevent lateral deviation. Lateral force overstretches or tears them regardless of what angle the knee is bent to.

Common mistake Attempting to 'open' the knee joint laterally to force Lotus or similar positions is a direct path to collateral ligament injury. Internal rotation of a bent knee is acceptable; lateral deviation never is.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. О раскрытии суставов

Anatomy

Understand that muscles produce movement by contracting, not by lengthening. The biceps shortens to bend the elbow; the quadriceps shortens to extend the knee. Stop trying to stretch muscles — instead, learn to use them.

why · mistakehide

Why Years of passive stretching train the body to yield under load rather than generate force, producing weak, injury-prone mobility.

Common mistake Assuming tightness means a muscle must be stretched; the root cause is nearly always failure to coordinate antagonist pairs.

Source Принципы биомеханики в йоге. Анатолий Зенченко. · Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Йога как она есть. Правда без иллюзий

Anatomy

Instead of stretching a muscle, create coordinated, balanced interaction between antagonist pairs. Every muscle in the body has its direct opposite — when those two are in harmonious tone, smooth movement occurs within the natural range, and that is all you need.

why · mistakehide

Why The body's full natural range of motion is accessible once antagonist pairs coordinate well; no additional stretching is required.

Common mistake Blaming the muscle for being 'too short' when the real problem is a wrong or absent command from the nervous system.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. О методике Ишвара-йога. 3 часть · Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Йога как она есть. Правда без иллюзий · Анатолий Зенченко о важности бандх в практике йоги

Anatomy

Always collect the spine first. Arms and legs have nothing to attach to until the spine is integral and properly aligned — establish spinal wholeness before trying to organize the limbs.

why · mistakehide

Why The spine is the central axis; limb function depends entirely on the quality of their attachment to that axis.

Common mistake Trying to fix arm or leg position while the spine is still fragmented or misaligned.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Позвоночник - основа внутренней целостности.

Anatomy

Never create a breaking point — a kink or local compression — in the spine. In any position, maintain a smooth, controlled line through the entire length of the vertebral column. The primary task in every asana is to control spinal position.

why · mistakehide

Why A breaking point in the spine severs the functional connection between body segments, and the surrounding muscles will reflexively spasm to lock that zone.

Common mistake Opposing one body segment against another — for example, twisting so that the upper and lower halves rotate against each other — creating a compression point.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Позвоночник - основа внутренней целостности. · Джаландхара Бандха. Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар выходного дня в Киеве.

Anatomy

Between mobility and connection, always choose connection. A mobile but structurally disconnected joint is dangerous; a connected joint that moves less is safe and workable.

why · mistakehide

Why When a joint loses structural integrity, the body automatically guards it with pain and muscular spasm as a defense mechanism.

Common mistake Deepening range of motion at the expense of joint stability and integrity.

Source О целостности в йоге. Анатолий Зенченко.

Anatomy

Your legs are the body's accumulators. When the legs work correctly, the pelvic organs function well and the gastrointestinal tract works properly. When the leg muscles are inactive, the pelvic organs are the first to suffer.

why · mistakehide

Why The large muscle pump of the legs drives venous return and lymphatic drainage, directly supporting circulation and visceral function of the pelvis and abdomen.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Open Air 2015. Киев. Практика

Anatomy

The iliopsoas controls the position of the pelvis. When the pelvis is correctly positioned through psoas engagement, the lumbar releases, the glutes activate, and the legs can do everything they are designed to do — it is a cascade.

why · mistakehide

Why Pelvic position is the root of leg function; no amount of direct glute or quad work substitutes for establishing correct psoas-driven pelvic alignment first.

Common mistake Trying to activate the glutes or legs directly without first establishing correct pelvic position through the psoas.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О правильной работе ног.

Anatomy

In every movement, integrity — a felt sense of wholeness and continuous connection between body parts and the center — always takes priority over range of motion. The body will grant you full access to your natural mobility only when it trusts you are not about to break something.

why · mistakehide

Why The body's protective reflex contracts muscles when it senses disintegration. Working from integrity first removes that protective tension and unlocks natural range of motion without force.

Common mistake Pushing into range of motion without first establishing structural coherence — the body contracts to protect itself, which practitioners mistake for tightness they then try to stretch further.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар под Киевом. Зачем нужны базовые асаны и что такое джаландхара бандха. · Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара-йога - йога внутренней целостности · Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Аспекты анатомии и физиологии в йоге. Связки и сухожилия

Anatomy

Do not try to stretch ligaments or tendons — they are like steel cables: elastic but not extensible. Your natural joint mobility is sufficient for every asana. Work with correct muscular engagement, not with attempts to elongate connective tissue.

why · mistakehide

Why Ligaments are structural anchors keeping bones from separating; tendons are fixed muscle attachment points. Neither is designed to lengthen. Pulling on them risks joint instability rather than increasing useful range.

Common mistake Believing that yoga 'stretching' means elongating tendons and ligaments to gain range — this is anatomically impossible and injurious.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Аспекты анатомии и физиологии в йоге. Связки и сухожилия

Anatomy

A joint has two opposing jobs: stability (keeping parts from separating) and mobility. When forced to choose, the body always chooses stability. Give joints mobility only in their natural direction and position — pain in a joint signals a wrong direction or wrong position, not a need to push harder.

why · mistakehide

Why The body is wired to protect joint integrity above all. Pain in a joint is not a signal to push further; it is the body saying the direction or position is wrong.

Common mistake Interpreting joint pain as a sign that you need to open or stretch more, rather than reconsidering the direction and position of the movement.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Аспекты анатомии и физиологии в йоге. Связки и сухожилия

Anatomy

The functional chain runs: diaphragm → psoas major → iliacus → quadriceps → adductors. If any link is missing — a slumped spine, an inactive diaphragm — the intended downstream muscle will not fire even if you consciously try to activate it.

why · mistakehide

Why The psoas responds to the diaphragm; the quadriceps to the psoas; the adductors to the quadriceps. This is the physiological cascade that makes coordinated movement possible.

Common mistake Trying to directly activate a downstream muscle (e.g. the quadriceps for a forward fold) while the spine is collapsed or the diaphragm is not engaged.

Source О взаимосвязи причин и симптомов. Анатолий Зенченко. · Мула бандха. Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога. · Диафрагма. Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар выходного дня в Киеве.

Anatomy

The diaphragm and the psoas major interweave at the thoracolumbar junction. When that junction is kinked or locked, opening the diaphragm directly resolves the kink — no external manipulation required.

why · mistakehide

Why Because these two muscles share the same junction, tension in one creates tension in the other. Releasing the diaphragm decompresses the psoas at their intersection.

Common mistake Trying to manually stretch or massage the lumbar area when the real cause is a non-functioning diaphragm.

Source Диафрагма. Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар выходного дня в Киеве.

Anatomy

A muscle is a piston — it contracts and extends, nothing more. Do not stretch muscles, ligaments, or tendons. The natural range of the tissue is its full range; going beyond it creates uncontrolled hypermobility in the joint.

why · mistakehide

Why Over-lengthened connective tissue loses the ability to stabilize a joint. The joint then moves outside its controlled range, leading to instability and injury.

Common mistake Treating yoga as a stretching exercise — pulling muscles and ligaments as if length itself were the goal.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Анатомия и физиология йоги. Мышцы и кожа · Анатолий Зенченко. Open Air 2015. Киев. Теория

Anatomy

Do not pull the skin. The skin covers your body in exactly the amount needed. If you pull it one direction, a fold forms elsewhere. The skin plays no role in building an asana — leave it alone.

why · mistakehide

Why The skin has no role in building or deepening an asana. Pulling it diverts attention from the actual work.

Common mistake Consciously or unconsciously tensioning the skin surface during posture adjustments.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Анатомия и физиология йоги. Мышцы и кожа

Anatomy

Focus on the transverse abdominis, not the rectus. To activate it, draw the navel toward the spine. Use the image of holding an orange with your navel, pressing it gently toward the spine — hold it through every position, but do not crush it.

why · mistakehide

Why The transverse abdominis creates intra-abdominal pressure and stabilizes the lumbar spine. The rectus (six-pack) is superficial and contributes nothing to postural stability.

Common mistake Training the rectus through crunches while the deep stabilizer stays inactive.

Source Пупок: работа с мышцами живота. Анатолий Зенченко

Anatomy

The center of the body is behind the navel, deep inside near the spine — where the umbilical cord connected you to life. To achieve wholeness in any asana, connect everything to this center and draw all parts of the body toward it.

why · mistakehide

Why Organizing movement around the anatomical center prevents fragmented action and creates a unified structural field the body can orient within.

Common mistake Initiating movements from peripheral segments (hands, feet, neck) without anchoring through the center first.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Понятие центра.

Anatomy

Do not try to 'stretch' the spine. Compressive force between vertebrae is enormous; what protects the discs is the cushioning action of the paraspinal muscles. Keep those muscles working — do not suppress their tone by collapsing or over-stretching.

why · mistakehide

Why The spinal joints are protected by active muscular support, not passive stretching. When muscles go slack, joint surfaces impact directly, accelerating disc degeneration.

Common mistake Doing 'spine-lengthening' exercises that suppress paraspinal tone in the belief that more space between vertebrae is inherently good.

Source Мула бандха. Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

03

The method of practice

How to actually work on the mat: wholeness over isolation, balance over force, and earning the nervous system's trust rep by rep until it stops protecting you from yourself.

Method

In every asana, designate something stable — the 'wall' — so something else can be mobile — the 'spring.' Either stabilize the pelvis to move the leg, or stabilize the leg to move the pelvis and spine.

why · mistakehide

Why A spring functions only when one end is anchored. The same muscle produces different movement depending on which end is fixed.

Common mistake Trying to increase range on both ends at once so effort dissipates.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 3

Method

Practice every asana with the entire body simultaneously — the principle of wholeness. If even one part is uncomfortable, work on all parts is compromised. A problem in the leg may have its root in the shoulder.

why · mistakehide

Why Muscles are like fish scales — if scales stick in one place, the whole fish cannot move harmoniously.

Common mistake Isolating practice to the problem area while ignoring the rest.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Объяснение сути методики Ишвара йога · Анатолий Зенченко. О внутренней целостности

Method

About 50% of the body's musculature forms one functional chain; the opposing 50% forms the other. In every asana, balance these two chains. This is not a strength task — it is a balancing task.

why · mistakehide

Why This reduces any asana to one question: which chain is overdominant and which underactivated? Restore equilibrium and the posture becomes accessible.

Common mistake Over-relying on one chain while leaving its opposite unengaged.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Объяснение сути методики Ишвара йога

Method

When you consistently maintain inner wholeness — gathering every joint, protecting your integrity in every position — the body gradually learns to trust you and protective tension diminishes on its own. You earn the body's cooperation, you do not force it.

why · mistakehide

Why The nervous system is protective by default; it releases only when it learns through repeated experience that you will not disintegrate the body.

Common mistake Expecting the body to open without first demonstrating trustworthiness, then resorting to force.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. О внутренней целостности

Method

Use twisting asanas to balance the right and left halves of the body. Spinal twists reveal and correct chronic left-right asymmetries that limit every other movement in your practice.

why · mistakehide

Why Uncorrected left-right asymmetries limit progress in forward bends, backbends, and inversions alike.

Common mistake Deprioritizing twists while asymmetries silently limit everything else.

Source Анатолий Зенченко о семинаре "Биомеханика асан"

Method

Don't use force — use precision. Technique means applying the minimum effort to get the maximum result. The correct approach is not 'try harder' but 'move more accurately.'

why · mistakehide

Why Brute force bypasses the neural coordination that is the actual goal of practice. Precision trains the nervous system's ability to send the right coordinated commands to the right muscles.

Common mistake Compensating for lack of technique with excessive muscular effort — pulling harder or straining more instead of identifying and using the correct muscle.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 1 · Тело: ключи к работе с телом в практике асан. Анатолий Зенченко

Method

Focus your attention on what does NOT work in your body. The places that don't activate are territory to reclaim — they are not participating in your yoga practice at all. Every asana is an opportunity to find those places and integrate them.

why · mistakehide

Why Repeating what already works reinforces existing patterns and bypasses disconnected areas. The non-responsive places represent body parts that have been functionally cut off from conscious neural control.

Common mistake Chasing the deepest version of a posture or comparing yourself to others — the more important work is in the places you cannot feel, not in impressive terminal ranges.

Source 20/05 Интенсив 3 уровня с Анатолием Зенченко. Рекомендации к практике. · Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Как устранить проблемы в практике

Method

Asana is a training position in which you learn to send correctly coordinated commands to specific muscle groups. The external shape is secondary — the inner coordination and neural communication between muscle groups is the actual purpose.

why · mistakehide

Why This is why yoga traditions noted that asana practice 'improves the functioning of the nervous system' — the body's coordination system is being rebuilt, not just stretched or strengthened.

Common mistake Fixating on the external appearance of a posture and comparing yourself to a photograph or to other students, rather than investigating the inner coordination each pose requires.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 1

Method

Asanas can be classified into 5 quality categories, and every asana belongs to all 5. Use this classification like Lego: understand what quality each asana develops, and build sequences from simple to complex that are ideal for a specific student at a specific moment — adjusting as they progress.

why · mistakehide

Why A sequence built on this classification ensures each posture prepares the neural and muscular conditions for the next, allowing safe and logical progression for any individual student.

Common mistake Teaching a random or aesthetically driven sequence without considering the logical progression of neural complexity and physiological preparation for each specific student.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. О методике Ишвара-йога. 4 часть

Method

In Ishvara Yoga, the rule is: do not stretch the skin, muscles, ligaments, or tendons; do not 'open' joints; do not bend bones. Every asana — even the most complex — can be mastered without pain, without stretching, and without trauma.

why · mistakehide

Why Any natural position of the body can be reached through correct neural commands and proper coordination, not through mechanical force on tissue.

Common mistake The belief that you need to 'stretch' to become more flexible.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Лекция о методике Ишвара-йога. 2 часть

Method

The main reason you cannot do an asana is that your brain cannot give the correct command to your body and coordinate its parts — not the length of your legs, not the length of your ligaments, not how much you torture your tissues.

why · mistakehide

Why Movement is generated by neural commands to the motor centers; if the signal is incorrect or fragmented, no amount of stretching will produce the desired position.

Common mistake Attributing inability to the body ('my hamstrings are too tight') and responding by stretching.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Лекция о методике Ишвара-йога. 2 часть

Method

Perceiving the body as a collection of separate parts — 'this is me' (torso), 'and those are my legs over there' — creates an internal conflict during asana. You must experience the body as one unified whole at all times.

why · mistakehide

Why When you treat a body part as 'other', you create a mental split that prevents the coordinated neural firing required for the asana.

Common mistake 'I am trying to reach my legs, but my hamstrings are blocking me' — fighting part of yourself.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Лекция о методике Ишвара-йога. 2 часть

Method

When you reach the limit of your range — that moment where the body simply stops, even without pain — do not force further. Instead, bring that area into tone, allow the tension to dissolve, and then the movement continues on its own.

why · mistakehide

Why The body stops not because tissue is too short, but because the nervous system has reached its safety threshold; bringing the area into deliberate tone signals safety and the reflex releases.

Common mistake Forcing past the stoppage point and waiting for the body to 'adapt'.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О том, как расширить зону комфорта, не покидая ее.

Method

Go to the boundary of your current possibilities but do not break them. Expand the boundary very gently from the inside — do not fight yourself.

why · mistakehide

Why Forcing beyond conscious awareness produces injury and traumatic compensation because there is no proprioceptive feedback to guide the force.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О том, как расширить зону комфорта, не покидая ее.

Method

An asana is not a shape — it is a process of directed movement. Even when you physically cannot move a single millimeter further, continue creating that movement from within, connecting the muscles more tightly, so that tomorrow the millimeter becomes possible.

why · mistakehide

Why The internal muscular effort in a static position continues to train neural pathways and build the coordinated engagement that eventually allows the movement to manifest physically.

Common mistake Passively holding a shape while waiting for the body to 'relax into it'.

Source Что такое асана? Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар выходного дня в Киеве.

Method

Wholeness means all parts of the body connected like drops of mercury merging — complete, yet fully mobile. The more you feel the connections between vertebrae and maintain those connections during movement, the more freedom the body grants you.

why · mistakehide

Why When the body senses that you are maintaining integrity, it gradually trusts you with greater range of motion.

Common mistake Assuming that more flexibility requires more looseness — in fact, greater connectivity and control produce greater range.

Source Анатолий Зенченко о целостности · Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Йога внутренней целостности.

Method

If you cannot yet feel your body well enough to maintain internal coherence, do not attempt complex asanas — they will only twist and compensate you further. Work on simpler poses until the felt sense is there.

why · mistakehide

Why Complex asanas amplify existing asymmetries and compensatory patterns.

Common mistake Attempting advanced asanas before having the body awareness to do them with integrity.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Йога внутренней целостности.

Method

Every practitioner has their own 'favourite places' — recurring problem areas that stay in the same location. Find your biggest one and address it first; once resolved, address the next biggest. Do not work on small problems while ignoring large ones.

why · mistakehide

Why Like a boat with multiple holes — if you patch the smallest one while ignoring the largest, you sink.

Common mistake Jumping from technique to technique while the major structural issue remains unresolved.

Source Дафрагма: значение и функции в работе с телом. Анатолий Зенченко

Method

Motor centers responsible for movement are located in the subcortex, distributed across different brain regions. Yoga trains you to send deliberate volitional impulses from the cortex to multiple subcortical regions simultaneously and integrate them into coordinated movement.

why · mistakehide

Why Complex positions require the conscious mind to simultaneously direct multiple subcortical motor programs; this is literally brain training.

Source Взаимодействие сознания и подсознания. Анатолий Зенченко.

Method

When creating any movement — forward fold, backbend, or twist — continuously monitor whether you are over-tensing and whether you are tensing the right thing. The ability to remain relaxed while producing directed movement is a core skill.

why · mistakehide

Why Unnecessary tension wastes energy, blocks the primary movement, and masks proprioceptive feedback.

Common mistake Generic full-body bracing instead of precise activation of only what is needed.

Source Online-практика с Анатолием Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Method

Find a reasonable compromise between your desire to do everything immediately and the actual capabilities you have right now. Use intelligence, not force — if you are struggling, you may have chosen too high a level, or you do not yet understand the technique.

why · mistakehide

Why The body changes progressively; forcing a level beyond current capacity creates compensation patterns.

Common mistake Suffering through a level that is too hard instead of stepping back to a simpler version.

Source Ішвара йога. Анатолій Зенченко. Основи йоги. Питання для початківця

Method

The goal of practice is NOT to stretch muscles, ligaments, or tendons, and NOT to 'open' joints. The goal is to establish precise, coordinated, synchronized work of all parts of the body in any position in space.

why · mistakehide

Why When all parts of the body work together correctly, the body naturally arrives at the correct position without force. Injuries occur when the wrong parts carry the load.

Common mistake Measuring progress by how far you can stretch or how deep you can go in a pose.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О методике · Как создать целостность любого сустава. Анатолий Зенченко.

Method

There are 10 internal principles of body work, and they apply equally and identically to every single asana — standing, inverted, backbend, forward fold, arm balance. Learn these 10; forget trying to memorize hundreds of pose-specific rules.

why · mistakehide

Why In a difficult asana you often forget even to breathe — you will never remember 387 pose-specific rules. Universal principles remain accessible under stress.

Common mistake Trying to memorize pose-specific alignment cues for each asana separately instead of internalizing universal principles.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О сильных и умных людях · Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О методике

Method

Find the exact boundary of your current ability — where natural movement stops. Bring yourself to that boundary and then gently, gradually expand it from the inside. Never jump over your limits or try to break through them by force.

why · mistakehide

Why Forcing past the limit triggers the body's protective reflexes (stabilization, bracing) and leads to injury. Gradual expansion trains the nervous system to allow new ranges without triggering those reflexes.

Common mistake Chasing the final pose seen in a photo or following sequences designed for someone else's body; treating intensity as a measure of progress.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О сильных и умных людях

Method

When natural movement ends, pause. Then — consciously, with attention — activate the specific muscles that will continue the movement. Do not tense to overcome resistance. Feel where the movement stopped and what needs to engage before taking the next step.

why · mistakehide

Why Tensing to push past the limit activates the wrong (compensating) muscles and masks the movement problem rather than resolving it, creating patterns of dysfunction and eventual injury.

Common mistake Immediately tensing to continue when movement stops — using brute force, trying to push through resistance.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 2 · Асаны без боли. Анатолий Зенченко

Method

Regular asana practice performed correctly strongly develops the brain by forcing it to build new neural connections. Intelligence is not determined by brain size or cell count, but by the richness of connections between neurons — exactly as muscles grow when given a load they cannot yet handle.

why · mistakehide

Why Unusual proprioceptive demands of yoga (precise, unfamiliar movement patterns) are non-template challenges for the nervous system — they require new inter-neuronal pathways, which is how the brain develops.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О развитии мозга

Method

Learn to notice the moment when movement stops — before any sensation of stretch or pain appears. That cessation of movement is your earliest and clearest signal that something is not activating. At that point, find the inactive muscle, engage it, and movement will resume. Never wait for pain — that signal is already three steps too late.

why · mistakehide

Why The body communicates through progressive signals: movement stops → compensatory tension appears → discomfort → pain. Acting at the first signal allows smooth correction; acting only at pain means you ignored multiple earlier opportunities.

Common mistake The three levels of insensitivity: (1) movement stops and you push through anyway; (2) you can feel yourself tensing to force it but continue; (3) you wait until it genuinely hurts. All three represent degrees of not listening to the body.

Source Ответы на вопросы. Анатолий Зенченко. Методика Ишвара йога.

Method

Use two criteria to judge whether your practice is correct: external — movement continues in the direction you intend; internal — the sensation of pulling, pain, or compensatory tension disappears. When movement blocks, something is acting as a stabilizer that should be a mobilizer — find it, activate the correct muscle, and let movement resume.

why · mistakehide

Why Compensation patterns mean wrong muscles tense to substitute for inactive correct ones. The solution is not to stretch the tense muscle but to activate its missing functional partner.

Source Ответы на вопросы. Анатолий Зенченко. Методика Ишвара йога.

Method

We do not stretch muscles — we stop tensing the wrong ones and begin activating those we have been ignoring. The sensation of 'stretch' is the consequence of one muscle contracting while its antagonist is not activating to balance it. Activate the neglected antagonist and the 'stretched' muscle releases on its own.

why · mistakehide

Why Muscles exist in reciprocal inhibition pairs: when one contracts, the opposing one is neurologically inhibited into release. The apparent need to stretch is usually actually a need to activate the antagonist.

Common mistake Pulling on a hamstring to lengthen it creates more protective contraction. Instead, actively contract the quadriceps and give the command to straighten the leg through the front surface of the thigh — the hamstring releases automatically.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Два способа взаимодействия с телом

Method

Begin by learning to eliminate your personal asymmetry in simple, symmetrical poses before attempting complex or asymmetrical ones. Use a figure-8 movement of the pelvis as a diagnostic tool — it will quickly reveal which side engages less, and from that you can trace the root cause (often a psoas or diaphragm asymmetry, not a leg issue).

why · mistakehide

Why An asymmetrical body in an asymmetrical asana compounds the existing imbalance. Simple symmetrical poses are the clearest mirror for diagnosing what is actually not working and on which side.

Common mistake Jumping into asymmetrical asanas before addressing baseline asymmetry can make the imbalance progressively worse — some practitioners work for years and become more crooked rather than less.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О внутренней симметрии (и асимметрии).

Method

The asana is not the goal — internal symmetry is the goal. Every asana you work with is just a tool for finding and correcting your personal asymmetry. When internal symmetry is achieved, the asana form follows naturally without forcing.

why · mistakehide

Why Internal asymmetry at the level of the psoas, diaphragm, or pelvis propagates through every asana. Resolving the root asymmetry corrects all its downstream consequences simultaneously.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О внутренней симметрии (и асимметрии).

Technique

Do not try to 'open' joints — collect and stabilize them. In every asana, your intention should be to draw the joint surfaces toward each other and maintain that integral connection through the full range of motion. When you demonstrate consistent care for a joint, the subconscious nervous system progressively allows the joint's full natural mobility.

why · mistakehide

Why The body has restricted your joint mobility as a protective response to perceived careless handling. Demonstrating care and stability — even in difficult positions — changes the subconscious assessment and removes the protective lock.

Common mistake Forcing a joint to its end range without first establishing stability signals danger to the subconscious, which responds by locking down mobility even further as protection.

Source Работа с суставами. Анатолий Зенченко. · Анатолий Зенченко. О раскрытии суставов

Technique

Do not attempt to straighten the thoracic spine by squeezing the muscles between the shoulder blades. Those muscles attach the arms to the thorax — they do not and cannot determine thoracic position. Squeezing them adds more tension to already-tense tissue without changing spinal shape, and the position reverts within seconds every time.

why · mistakehide

Why Thoracic position is determined by the integrated state of the diaphragm, rib cage, and spinal extensors — not by the rhomboids or middle trapezius. These are arm-attachment muscles, not spine-position muscles.

Common mistake The common cue 'squeeze your shoulder blades together' creates chronic overload in the rhomboids and middle trapezius while never addressing the actual cause of thoracic kyphosis.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О том, как не надо выпрямлять спину.

Method

Treat every asana as a movement in progress — a process — not as a static shape to achieve. Even when your body cannot advance by a single millimeter, your brain and nervous system must continue pressing toward the movement.

why · mistakehide

Why A static 'shape' mindset leads to passive holding and injury; a movement/process mindset recruits correct motor patterns and keeps the body cooperative.

Common mistake Fixing attention on achieving a final shape, then collapsing into a passive hold once you arrive.

Source Принципы биомеханики в йоге. Анатолий Зенченко. · Анатолий Зенченко. О методике Ишвара-йога. 3 часть

Method

When you encounter muscular tension anywhere in the body, do not fight it or try to force through it. The body created that tension deliberately to protect a weak or uncoordinated zone. Activate the opposing, dormant muscles, and the protective tension will release on its own.

why · mistakehide

Why Forced release of protective tension without activating the underlying weak muscles removes the body's safeguard without supplying any structural replacement — injury follows.

Common mistake Treating tightness as an obstacle to overcome rather than as information about which muscles need to be activated.

Source Анатолий Зенченко о важности бандх в практике йоги · О целостности в йоге. Анатолий Зенченко.

Method

The first five of Ishvara yoga's ten principles all describe how to create internal integrity — how to keep the arms, legs, torso, and head unified as one body in any position in space. Your body does not know you are doing Trikonasana; it perceives it as an attempt to tear it apart, and it will defend itself until you establish integrity.

why · mistakehide

Why Without internal integrity, the body uses muscular tension to protect itself against every asana, blocking both progress and ease.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. О методике Ишвара-йога. 3 часть

Method

Yoga unites the conscious and the subconscious mind by building new neural connections between them. In any complex asana, neither conscious will alone nor subconscious reflex alone can execute the movement — you must create coordinated motor pathways that link both.

why · mistakehide

Why Asana practice is neurologically high-level work: it requires simultaneously generating conscious volitional impulses from the cortex and integrating them with subcortical motor reflexes through new synaptic pathways.

Source Анатолий Зенченко о важности бандх в практике йоги

Method

Do not attempt complex asanas until you can genuinely feel the internal work — bandhas, muscular tone, the sense of being in control — in simple ones. All complex asanas are combinations of elements from simple ones, so a well-built foundation makes everything else accessible.

why · mistakehide

Why Without internal sensitivity, complex asanas work against you. Time spent on foundational postures with full inner awareness unlocks depth in all other asanas simultaneously.

Common mistake Rushing to impressive shapes before the internal architecture is established — the complex asana will simply injure you.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар под Киевом. Зачем нужны базовые асаны и что такое джаландхара бандха.

Method

In any asana, work sequentially: establish one action (for example, Mula Bandha), hold it, and only once you have a little free attention do you add the next element. Never try to apply every cue at once.

why · mistakehide
