Why Attention is limited. Sequential layering ensures each component is actually established rather than merely attempted.

Common mistake Trying to apply every cue simultaneously from the start — nothing gets properly established.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар под Киевом. Зачем нужны базовые асаны и что такое джаландхара бандха.

Method

The most important criterion of any asana — simple or complex — is internal: do you feel GOOD in it? The external shape is secondary. If you are uncomfortable, you are either not ready for that asana or doing it incorrectly. Expand your comfort zone without ever leaving it.

why · mistakehide

Why Comfort is not laziness — it is the signal that the nervous system is coordinating correctly. Pain achieved in a shape does harm, not good.

Common mistake Prioritizing the external look of the asana over inner sensation — grinding through discomfort and treating it as 'working through tightness'.

Source Что такое асана? Анатолий Зенченко. · Анатолий Зенченко. О методике Ишвара-йога. 1 часть

Method

Move your awareness to the INSIDE of the body — not to the skin surface or the external shape, but to the interior muscles, joints, and sensations. Once you are genuinely inside, the body stops blocking your movement and far more becomes possible without force.

why · mistakehide

Why Most people sense only the body's surface because the interior feels unfamiliar and vaguely threatening. Interior attention is what allows conscious access to deep muscles the brain has not previously learned to control.

Common mistake Focusing on how the asana looks from the outside, or on the stretch sensation at the skin and superficial fascia, rather than sensing what is happening from the inside.

Source Йога - это гимнастика для мозга. Анатолий Зенченко. · Что такое асана? Анатолий Зенченко.

Method

Where you feel pain or pulling is a symptom, not the cause. The cause is always a muscle that should be in tone but is not. Consciously move attention away from the loud painful sensation toward the muscle that must activate — when it does, the symptomatic tension releases.

why · mistakehide

Why The nervous system always prioritizes the loudest signal. While attention stays on the pain, you cannot sense the quieter absence of tone in the causal muscle.

Common mistake Focusing all attention on the site of pain and trying to 'work through' it directly, missing the upstream cause.

Source О взаимосвязи причин и симптомов. Анатолий Зенченко.

Method

First criterion of a correct asana: you are ready to jump at any moment. Not too tense, not too relaxed — the state of a half-compressed spring, like a cat about to pounce. Too tight, you can't jump; too loose, you can't jump either.

why · mistakehide

Why This balance between kinetic and potential energy indicates that all joints are gathered, all muscles are in functional tone, and the body is organized as a unified whole.

Common mistake Holding asanas in rigid locked-down tension, or collapsing into passive flexibility — both prevent readiness.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Критерий правильности выполнения асан. · Критерий собранности суставов или как подпрыгнуть в Вирасане. Анатолий Зенченко.

Method

Second criterion: if someone rotated you in any direction in space, the internal structure of your position would be preserved. Test it — imagine being tipped forward, sideways, upside down. Does your organization hold?

why · mistakehide

Why Orientation-independence proves the structure comes from inner integrity, not from propping against gravity in one direction.

Common mistake Building the shape relative to the floor only, so the organization collapses the moment the relationship to gravity changes.

Source Анатолий Зенченко, второй критерий целостности

Method

The two things the brain cannot yet do: (1) perceive the body as a whole instead of disconnected fragments, and (2) create coordinated co-contraction of antagonist muscle pairs. Solve these two and any asana becomes accessible.

why · mistakehide

Why All difficulty in asana traces back to one of these two failures. Every technique in the method addresses one or both.

Common mistake Fixing each asana separately with pose-specific corrections instead of addressing the perceptual and neuromuscular root.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Open Air 2015. Киев. Теория

Method

There are 10 universal principles and every one applies to every asana without exception. There is no separate list of 300 corrections for one pose and 200 for another — just 10. Understand them and you understand every asana.

why · mistakehide

Why A universal framework lets teacher and student diagnose any pose with the same vocabulary, rather than memorizing endless pose-specific rules.

Common mistake Treating each asana as needing its own unique set of alignment rules, which fragments understanding.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. О принципах Ишвара йоги. · Анатолий Зенченко. Open Air 2015. Киев. Теория

Method

Build training programs from simple to complex and tailor them to the individual — their level, injuries, and goals. No single sequence is ideal for everyone; what is beneficial for one person can be harmful for another.

why · mistakehide

Why Individual variation in anatomy, injury history, and neurological development means a standardized sequence poorly fits most people.

Common mistake Following a fixed universal sequence as if it were correct for all bodies at all stages.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Open Air 2015. Киев. Теория

04

Breath and the locks

Breath is the conductor; the locks are the fine tuning — the deep, quiet control that connects the center of the body to everything else.

Breath

Make your inhale long, smooth, and calm so that air reaches every alveolus. Make your exhale equally long and smooth to fully extract CO2. This is the mechanism of proper gas exchange.

why · mistakehide

Why The brain consumes approximately 30% of all oxygen and is the first organ to suffer from deficiency; full exhalation clears CO2 so the next inhale is genuinely productive.

Common mistake Short, shallow, or rapid breathing — even if you are in oxygen-rich air, breathing incorrectly means you cannot extract what is there.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О важности дыхания

Breath

Regular pranayama practice — not just occasional deep breathing — rewires your default breathing pattern so that deeper, fuller breathing becomes your second nature throughout the day.

why · mistakehide

Why Breathing quality directly affects both physiology and state of consciousness — and it is happening constantly, unlike eating or sleeping.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О важности дыхания

Breath

Do not try to breathe deeply in complex asanas. Do not do complex asanas while attempting deep pranayama. They are separate practices — flies separately, meatballs separately.

why · mistakehide

Why In difficult asanas the thorax is compressed, and the breathing muscles are already fully occupied stabilizing the spine — there is no room for deep breath, and forcing it leads to uncontrolled shifts.

Common mistake Modern trend of combining advanced asana with pranayama in the same moment.

Source Как дышать в асанах? Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Bandhas

Think of your entire body as one tube, assembled and sealed by the bandhas. The body is 70-80% water: when the tube is whole and integral, that water distributes evenly downward through the legs and arms into the ground, creating a stable, living structure. Bandhas are not something you do in certain poses — they are the permanent internal glue of the body.

why · mistakehide

Why A body that is not assembled as one unit has weak points where energy, structural support, and force transmission leak out. Integrity of the tube distributes load evenly across all surfaces.

Common mistake Applying bandhas only in specific poses (e.g., inversions) or treating them as separate abdominal or pelvic floor contractions rather than a whole-body phenomenon.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О целостности. · Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О работе мускулатуры тела.

Breath

Direct your inhalation specifically into the BACK of the diaphragm — imagine inflating the area behind you, between the lower back and the lower floating ribs. This activates the posterior diaphragm, whose two crura descend alongside the spine and attach at the level of L2-L3. This is the most mechanically important part of the diaphragm for spinal control.

why · mistakehide

Why The diaphragm's posterior crura make it a direct stabilizer of the lumbar spine. Most people breathe only into the front of the diaphragm and never engage this posterior lever — which is why so many have unstable lumbar spines despite regular practice.

Common mistake Breathing only into the front of the chest or the front of the belly leaves the posterior crura inactive, which means the arms cannot properly attach to the torso and the shoulders chronically ride up toward the ears.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Задняя часть диафрагмы.

Breath

Breath retention (kumbhaka) trains your cells to use oxygen far more efficiently. When hyperventilation floods the blood with oxygen but the cells cannot absorb it (membrane receptors become saturated), then a breath hold creates the signal that forces cells to switch from a lazy, inefficient mode to a high-performance metabolic mode that generates significantly more energy.

why · mistakehide

Why Cellular efficiency is not just about oxygen availability but about receptor state and metabolic mode. The sequence of hyperventilation followed by retention exploits this: create a paradoxical cellular oxygen deficit, then resume breathing into cells that have switched to their efficient mode.

Common mistake Deep rapid breathing (hyperventilation) does NOT increase cellular oxygenation — it causes functional hypoxia by overloading membrane receptors so cells paradoxically cannot absorb the abundant oxygen in the blood.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Описание физиологических процессов во время дыхания

Breath

Practice longer, slower breathing — extend both your inhalation and exhalation. The longer your breathing cycle, the slower your heart rate, and the more efficiently your whole system operates. In yoga, the length of a person's life is held to be proportional to the total length of all their breath cycles.

why · mistakehide

Why Breathing rate and heart rate are directly coupled. A calm, long breath creates a calm heart. The heart is calculated to perform a fixed number of contractions over a lifetime; the more economically it beats, the longer it lasts.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Длиное дыхание продлевает жизнь

Bandhas

The three bandhas — Mula, Uddiyana, Jalandhara — are three parts of one whole. Engage one correctly and the other two follow automatically. Do not think of them as separate locks to be applied one at a time. Their collective purpose in asana practice is to unite the segments of the torso into one continuous integrated tube through which energy can flow freely.

why · mistakehide

Why Bandhas in asana function as a system of segmental spinal locks that create alignment and interoceptive coherence throughout the torso. Partial application undermines the whole system.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О бандхах.

Bandhas

The bandhas described in the Hatha Yoga Pradipika were designed for pranayama and mudra practices — they are far more complex techniques than the versions used in asana work. In Ishvara Yoga, the bandhas applied during asana are functional, adapted versions for spinal control. Jalandhara Bandha is not simply 'chin to chest' — that is a gross simplification of the original technique.

why · mistakehide

Why Confusing the asana versions with the pranayama versions leads to incorrect technique in one or both contexts.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О бандхах.

Breath

The diaphragm is both the primary breathing muscle and the largest muscle in the body. It also controls the position of the thoracic cage. Train it directly: on the inhale it descends and expands outward in all directions; on the exhale it rises and draws inward.

why · mistakehide

Why Most people have a poorly functioning diaphragm and compensate by moving the shoulders and chest — inefficient, preventing deep full breathing, and losing thoracic control.

Common mistake Rolling the shoulders up and down or collapsing the ribcage instead of allowing the diaphragm to drop and expand.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Физиология дыхания · О роли диафрагмы. Анатолий Зенченко. Методика Ишвара йога.

Bandhas

In asana practice, use bandhas as tools to control the key junction points of the body where major muscle groups interact — not merely as abstract energy locks. Controlling these points lets you feel and activate the large muscle groups that are normally dormant.

why · mistakehide

Why Major muscle groups can be switched on or off from these junctions; conscious control there is what makes coordinated movement possible.

Source Анатолий Зенченко о важности бандх в практике йоги

Breath

For pranayama, sit with pelvis, thorax, and head aligned on a single vertical line. The more precisely you establish this vertical balance, the less muscular effort is spent holding the position, and the more those spinal muscles are freed to assist the breath.

why · mistakehide

Why When the three blocks are precisely stacked, gravity stabilizes the structure automatically. Any deviation forces paraspinal muscles to compensate, stealing energy and attention from the breath.

Common mistake Sitting with the pelvis collapsed backward or the spine rounded — postural muscles then fight gravity rather than supporting the breath.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Правильное положение тела при дыхании

Breath

The diaphragm is the primary — and largest — breathing muscle. In most people it is blocked and cannot move downward or sideways, producing shallow upper-chest breathing that poorly ventilates the lower lung lobes. Free the diaphragm through correct posture and pranayama rather than training isolated 'belly' or 'chest' breathing patterns.

why · mistakehide

Why Air cannot be directed to only one region of the lungs anatomically. What matters is the diaphragm's full excursion — which is blocked by poor posture and tension, not by the wrong breathing 'technique'.

Common mistake Practising 'inhale belly forward, exhale belly back' as the central goal — this is an oversimplification that ignores why the diaphragm is restricted in the first place.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Правильное положение тела при дыхании

Breath

Pranayama works by creating a conscious dialogue with the subconscious. The average person operates on 3-10% of brain capacity. By consciously regulating breathing — a deeply subconscious process — you train the conscious and subconscious mind to communicate, integrate, and expand mutual awareness.

why · mistakehide

Why Breathing is one of very few processes that operates both automatically and consciously. This dual nature makes it an ideal bridge for training the conscious-subconscious integration that develops real self-awareness.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О сознании и подсознании · Йога: свобода, осознанность и ответственность. Анатолий Зенченко

05

The asana library

Every asana Anatoly breaks down, drawn. Tap a pose to open its specific technique. Ordered by how much attention he gives each.

Mula Bandha 8 points
+
Bandhas

Engage Mula Bandha to automatically activate the adductors of the inner thighs. Once the adductors carry tone, the subconscious recognizes the owner is controlling the leg — and grants permission for free, unrestricted movement.

why · mistakehide

Why The subconscious will not allow extreme leg range unless it senses the leg is 'claimed' and under control.

Common mistake Forcing leg range without establishing the inner root connection that signals safety.

Source О приводящих мышцах бёдер. Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар выходного дня в Киеве.

Bandhas

Engage mula bandha as a continuous process of maintaining conscious awareness in the pelvic floor — not a one-time hard squeeze. When I say 'more mula bandha,' I mean begin the engagement again, not squeeze harder.

why · mistakehide

Why Mula bandha connects the torso to the legs and places the pelvic-leg junction within conscious awareness, enabling the muscles of both trunk and legs to cooperate. Without it, the body segments work in isolation.

Common mistake Over-clenching the gluteals when engaging mula bandha — this blocks access to all other leg and hip muscles. The adductors engage with mula bandha; the gluteals should remain free and relaxed.

Source Мула бандха. Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар выходного дня в Киеве.

Bandhas

Mula Bandha is not achieved by consciously squeezing the perineum — it arises automatically when the iliopsoas and the quadriceps/adductors perform their coordinated pelvic counter-rotation. When the tailbone moves back and the iliac wings move forward, the pelvic floor is stretched in all four directions and naturally comes into tone.

why · mistakehide

Why The pubococcygeus spans between the two large muscle groups like a hammock under tension — it is stretched and toned by their coordinated action, not by being separately contracted.

Common mistake Trying to do Mula Bandha by focusing only on squeezing the perineum treats the symptom and ignores the cause. Without proper action of the large muscles, no amount of perineal effort produces real Mula Bandha.

Source Подвздошно поясничная мышца. Подробный разбор. Анатолий Зенченко · Корневой замок. Мулабандха. Анатолий Зенченко

Bandhas

To trigger Mula Bandha through a small control point that activates the large muscles: women — gently engage the vaginal muscles at the depth of the cervix (approximately one middle finger's depth inward); men — activate the perineal muscles in the area between the anus and the base of the scrotum. Either activation reflexively recruits the large pelvic and spinal stabilizers.

why · mistakehide

Why These small trigger points act as neural gateways. Their subtle engagement sets off a chain reaction that activates the larger structures — this is the efficient route, using a small muscle to coordinate two major muscle groups.

Common mistake Do not grip or clench hard — only a gentle engagement at the trigger point is needed to initiate the reflex chain.

Source Подвздошно поясничная мышца. Подробный разбор. Анатолий Зенченко

Bandhas

Use any of three cues to activate Mula Bandha — they all engage the same perineal muscles: (1) create a directed movement from the perineum upward along the spine toward the center of the belly; (2) try to draw the femoral heads toward each other; (3) try to bring the sacrum and the pubic symphysis toward each other.

why · mistakehide

Why Different students respond to different proprioceptive cues. All three actions recruit the same pelvic floor complex from different starting points of body awareness.

Common mistake Squeezing the gluteal muscles — this is not Mula Bandha and blocks the correct deep pelvic engagement.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар выходного дня в Киеве. Мула Бандха.

Bandhas

Mula Bandha is not simply squeezing the anus — it is the point of interaction between the psoas major and the quadriceps. For men: draw the base of the penis and the testicles upward toward the pelvis. For women: bring awareness to the vaginal muscles at the depth of the cervix.

why · mistakehide

Why This zone is where the muscles that control lumbar-pelvic position meet the muscles that control leg movement. Activating mula bandha links these two major functional groups.

Common mistake Focusing only on squeezing the anus — this often leaves the adductors and iliacus disengaged, so the pelvis is not fully stabilized.

Source Мула бандха. Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Bandhas

The test for correct mula bandha is that the adductor muscles of the inner thighs come into tone when you engage it. If your gluteal muscles tense up instead, you are engaging something else — not mula bandha.

why · mistakehide

Why The adductors attach to the pelvis and stabilize it from tipping forward. Their automatic activation confirms that the psoas-quadriceps interaction at the perineal zone is correctly engaged.

Common mistake Tensing the gluteal muscles while trying to engage mula bandha — a common substitution that bypasses the stabilizing function entirely.

Source Мула бандха. Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Bandhas

All three sphincters of the pelvic floor fire together, but the anus is secondary. The primary focus is the central perineum. Pulling primarily at the anus tends to leave the iliacus and adductors out of the circuit — that is Ashvini Mudra, a separate technique.

why · mistakehide

Why Ashvini Mudra (anus contraction) is a separate technique. Mula Bandha targets the deeper integration of the pelvic floor with the psoas and adductors, not the rectal sphincter.

Common mistake Confusing Ashvini Mudra (anus squeeze) with Mula Bandha, and practicing only the anus contraction.

Source Мула бандха. Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Uddiyana Bandha 8 points
+
Bandhas

In Uddiyana Bandha, draw the navel deeply toward the spine and maximize the full range of diaphragm travel — up, down, and sideways. Fully relax the outer abdominal muscles so they do not interfere with deep core participation.

why · mistakehide

Why This creates a vacuum in the body's center that draws lymph and fluids inward, massages organs, and activates digestive fire.

Common mistake Holding the outer abdominal wall rigid, preventing the deep muscles from participating.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Как работает вакуумное втягивание - Уддияна бандха

Bandhas

Draw the navel toward the spine and slightly downward — not just 'suck in the belly.' This specific directed movement brings the psoas into tone and gives you control over the lumbar spine, the pelvis, and the connection of the legs to the trunk.

why · mistakehide

Why The psoas connects the lumbar vertebrae to the femur and is both a spinal stabilizer and hip flexor. Toning it via navel retraction allows the outer back musculature to remain relatively relaxed while providing precise internal spinal control.

Common mistake Confusing navel retraction with generic abdominal bracing or simply pulling the belly in — the movement must be directed specifically toward the spine and slightly downward to recruit the psoas.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Включить большие поясничные мышцы. · Тело: ключи к работе с телом в практике асан. Анатолий Зенченко · Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар под Киевом

Anatomy

Pull the navel toward the spine to bring the transverse abdominis into tone. This muscle wraps around all five lumbar vertebrae and when activated straightens the lumbar spine — without requiring the back muscles or glutes at all.

why · mistakehide

Why The transverse abdominis (not rectus or obliques) anchors the lumbar spine; activating it also reduces belly volume and pushes internal organs upward to give the diaphragm an anchor point.

Common mistake Trying to control the lower back with the glutes or with direct effort of the back extensors, rather than through core engagement.

Source Уддияна бандха. Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Bandhas

To perform Uddiyana Bandha, combine two actions: (1) pull the navel toward the spine, and (2) gently press the diaphragm downward — the same action you make naturally on the toilet, but without forcing it.

why · mistakehide

Why Pulling the navel in sends organs upward, pressing against the central tendon of the diaphragm; this gives the diaphragm the resistance it needs to engage and spread laterally.

Common mistake Forcing the action too hard — the goal is just enough engagement to release chronically tight back muscles and awaken muscles that have not been working for years.

Source Уддияна бандха. Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Anatomy

When internal organs are pushed upward by the transverse abdominis, they press against the central tendon of the diaphragm from below. This gives the diaphragm the anchor it needs to contract. Without this support, the diaphragm cannot engage.

why · mistakehide

Why The diaphragm's muscular fibers need a fixed point (the central tendon) to pull against; the upward pressure of the abdominal contents creates that anchor.

Source Уддияна бандха. Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Bandhas

In Uddiyana Bandha during asana practice, do not push the navel outward or press it hard — instead, imagine you are inside the abdominal cavity and pulling the navel toward the spine from within, as if drawing a hook inward. The degree of engagement scales with the complexity of the movement: a small effort requires modest engagement; a maximum-difficulty movement requires maximum engagement.

why · mistakehide

Why The internal pulling sensation correctly recruits the deep transverse abdominis. The sensation of pushing or pressing tends to activate only the superficial rectus abdominis, which is not what is needed for spinal stabilization.

Common mistake The full vacuum Uddiyana Bandha described in the Hatha Yoga Pradipika is a completely different, far more advanced technique — do not confuse the asana-practice version with the classical pranayama version.

Source Уддияна бандха.О состоянии собранности в теле. Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар выходного дня в Киеве. · Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О бандхах.

Method

For deep abdominal self-massage: cup the hands and bring all eight fingers together into a wedge. Make a half-exhale, round the spine, then sink the finger-tips into the abdominal cavity in the direction of the spine and slowly knead — specifically searching for and working through tense or uncomfortable spots.

why · mistakehide

Why Rounding the spine on the exhale reduces abdominal wall tension, allowing deeper access to the visceral layers; fingers together form a narrower, more effective probe than spread hands.

Common mistake Placing the hands too far apart, or massaging on the inhale with a tense belly — you cannot reach the deeper layers this way.

Source Работа с животом. Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар в Индии 2017

Bandhas

Before performing the vacuum (full Uddiyana Bandha), first compress and lock the posterior portion of the diaphragm. The depth and appearance of the bandha is noticeably different when this posterior lock is applied versus when it is not.

why · mistakehide

Why Locking the posterior diaphragm seals the back portion of the abdominal cavity before drawing the front wall up and in, creating a deeper and more controlled vacuum.

Source Вакуумное втягивание живота. Анатолий Зенченко. Казантип.

Sirsasana 7 points
+
Technique

Tadasana is a balance asana, not a strength posture. Body weight passes through the bones; muscles merely keep the bones stacked. Handstand and headstand work on exactly the same principle — inverted balance, not tests of arm strength.

why · mistakehide

Why When bones are aligned, gravity transfers passively down the skeleton; muscles only maintain alignment — which is why you can stand in Tadasana for hours.

Common mistake Muscling through balance inversions with arm strength.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. В йоге нет силовых асан

Technique

Place the head not at the hairline but 4 fingers above it — at the fontanelle point where the four skull plates meet. Fully close the hand lock (base of palms touching each other). Raise the shoulders as HIGH as possible so the humerus is vertical, pressing into the floor through vertically stacked forearm, upper arm, and shoulder.

why · mistakehide

Why Standing on the fontanelle keeps the cervical spine in neutral — not hyperextended or compressed. Vertically stacked shoulders create a direct load path from the floor through the entire structure, putting the weight on the shoulder girdle rather than the neck.

Common mistake Placing the head at the hairline (compresses the cervical spine), leaving the hands in an open lock (unstable base), or not lifting the shoulders fully (causes the neck to bear the weight rather than the shoulder girdle).

Source Отстройка ширшасаны от Анатолия Зенченко

Technique

Entry sequence: place the head, raise the shoulders, bring the hips directly over the elbows, forget about the legs, push down into the floor with the elbows, open the diaphragm (uddiyana), rotate the pelvis upward — only then raise the legs. You are already pushing up into the ceiling before the legs go up.

why · mistakehide

Why Bringing the hips over the elbows shifts the center of gravity so that raising the legs requires almost no effort — they float up from the balanced position. Attempting to kick up before the hips are over the elbows requires great force and stresses the neck.

Common mistake Kicking or jumping the legs up before the hips are positioned over the elbows — this requires excessive force, causes compression of the cervical spine, and is the primary cause of headstand injuries.

Source Отстройка ширшасаны от Анатолия Зенченко

Philosophy

Do not confuse the name 'Viparita Karani' asana (a physical inverted posture) with the classical Viparita Karani Mudra technique (an energetic practice). Practicing headstand does not replicate the effects described for the classical mudra.

why · mistakehide

Why The classical mudra is an internal energy technique; it shares its name with an asana only by coincidence.

Common mistake Believing that headstand physically reverses aging because the name appears in classical texts.

Source О мифах в йоге. Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко.

Technique

In headstand, place the crown (the point 4 fingers above the hairline) at the CENTER of the triangle formed by your forearms, not at the apex. Put almost no weight into the head — most of the body's weight must rest in the elbows, forearms, and hands. After placing the head, push the shoulders to vertical before lifting anything else.

why · mistakehide

Why Vertical shoulders allow you to take the body's weight into the shoulder girdle instead of the cervical spine. If done correctly, you can lift your head off the floor while in the posture — the neck bears almost nothing.

Common mistake The 'banana' shape — collapsed lumbar spine and kinked neck — which creates cervical and intracranial pressure problems and prevents progression to forearm stand or handstand.

Source Ширшасана. Стойка на голове. Анатолий Зенченко

Technique

To enter headstand, first push the pelvis over the head with bent legs — forget about straightening the legs at first. Only extend the legs in the knees AFTER you can control the pelvis and lower back in that intermediate position. The legs must get tired more than anything else — that is the sign you are doing it correctly.

why · mistakehide

Why Control of pelvic and lumbar position is the structural prerequisite for safe headstand. Kicking up with straight legs masks the absence of this control and loads the neck instead of the shoulder girdle.

Common mistake Kicking up with straight legs before establishing pelvic control; legs not doing the work.

Source Ширшасана. Стойка на голове. Анатолий Зенченко

Philosophy

Simply inverting in a headstand does not build new neural connections. New pathways form only when the brain faces a problem it has never solved. The blood-flow effect is real, but neurological development requires genuine cognitive challenge — not just a position.

why · mistakehide

Why Neural plasticity is problem-driven. The brain must attempt solutions, fail, try differently — that iteration builds connectivity.

Common mistake Believing that any pose automatically develops the brain, so harder-looking poses equal more consciousness.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О стойке на голове и Йоге с большой буквы "Й".

Hanumanasana 5 points
+
Technique

For the front split, the key anatomical player is the iliopsoas: it controls the posterior tilt of the pelvis that blocks the fold. You must activate the iliopsoas to produce the anterior pelvic tilt — this is the primary prerequisite action. Without it, no amount of pulling at the hamstrings will work.

why · mistakehide

Why Most students try to pull at the posterior muscles while the actual restriction is a failure to orient the pelvis anteriorly. Until the pelvis tilts correctly via the iliopsoas, the posterior muscles remain in protective contraction and cannot release.

Common mistake The classic 'pull harder' approach — placing the foot on a block and pressing down repeatedly for years — targets the wrong mechanism and bypasses the necessary pelvic orientation.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 1

Technique

With the pelvis in a purely frontal (neutral) position, maximum hip abduction is only 45 degrees — not 90. To achieve a full transverse split, you must allow external rotation of the femur (change foot position) AND allow the pelvis to follow the leg.

why · mistakehide

Why The anatomy of the hip joint simply does not allow 90-degree abduction without femoral external rotation and pelvic accommodation — it is mechanics, not lack of flexibility.

Common mistake Trying to force the leg further out while the pelvis is tucked under — a recipe for joint damage.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Поперечный шпагат. Секреты освоения. Мифы и реальность

Technique

Do not try to 'open' or 'stretch' the hip joint — instead collect, connect, and center it. The solution for going deeper is better joint assembly, not more force.

why · mistakehide

Why A properly centered joint has more range of motion than a loose one — destabilizing a joint to 'open' it reduces the nervous system's willingness to allow movement.

Common mistake Repeatedly trying to 'open' the hip joint by forcing it.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Поперечный шпагат. Секреты освоения. Мифы и реальность

Technique

The main obstacle to the front split is almost never the hamstrings — it is the incorrect position of the pelvis. Correct the pelvic alignment first; until you do, no amount of work on the hamstrings will produce the split.

why · mistakehide

Why The pelvis is the root of the entire lower-body structure. A misaligned pelvis creates a chain of compensations that make full hip extension mechanically impossible regardless of hamstring length.

Common mistake Spending all practice time stretching the hamstrings while ignoring pelvic position and psoas engagement.

Source Анатолий Зенченко - методика Ишвара Йога. Класс 1/ Часть 2

Technique

The primary obstacle to the front split is not tight hamstrings or hip flexors — it is incorrect pelvic position. The legs grow out of the pelvis; if the pelvis is not in the correct orientation, the legs simply cannot achieve the required angle no matter how long you stretch them. Additionally, wrong head position and thoracic placement can block the split from a distance — address these upstream factors first.

why · mistakehide

Why The achievable hip angle is determined by the orientation of the pelvis. A pelvis without proper nutation cannot provide the angular orientation needed for the front leg to extend fully and the rear leg to lay flat.

Common mistake Spending years forcing the legs apart in a split without addressing pelvic position is futile and harmful — you are demanding from the legs what only correct pelvic alignment can provide.

Source Всё связано со всем. Анатолий Зенченко. · Ответы на вопросы. Анатолий Зенченко. Методика Ишвара йога.

Jalandhara Bandha 4 points
+
Bandhas

Jalandhara Bandha is not just a chin lock — it means bringing the anterior neck muscles into tone to balance the chronically over-contracted posterior neck muscles. Fix the thoracic cage position first; only then will the head sit correctly on top of it.

why · mistakehide

Why Constant spasm in the posterior cervical muscles combined with a poorly placed thoracic cage creates self-inflicted compression of the cervical vertebrae — nobody is hitting you there; you are doing it to yourself.

Common mistake Attempting to correct neck position without first correcting the placement and alignment of the thoracic cage.

Source Джаландхара Бандха. Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар выходного дня в Киеве.

Bandhas

Jalandhara Bandha is not a head position — it is control of the deep musculature at the cervico-thoracic junction regardless of where the head points. Keep the neck elongated in every head position; always draw the shoulders apart and lower the shoulder blades down.

why · mistakehide

Why Saying Jalandhara depends on head position is like saying Mula Bandha depends on the position of the legs — both are muscular engagements of deep structures, not joint angles.

Common mistake Believing you achieve Jalandhara only by tucking the chin to the chest and that it disappears whenever the head moves to any other position.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар под Киевом. Зачем нужны базовые асаны и что такое джаландхара бандха.

Bandhas

To activate Jalandhara Bandha, imagine you have swallowed a grape and it has lodged at the cervico-thoracic junction. Use the esophageal muscles and deep anterior neck muscles to hold it there — pressing it toward the spine. Also draw the sternal (jugular) notch toward the spine.

why · mistakehide

Why This cue activates the correct deep anterior cervical and esophageal muscles, which allows the large superficial throat and neck muscles to relax — releasing the grip they otherwise place on the posterior neck.

Common mistake Contracting the large superficial muscles of the throat or front of the neck — this immediately destroys Jalandhara because those muscles transfer tension to the back of the neck and overwhelm the deep ones.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар под Киевом. Зачем нужны базовые асаны и что такое джаландхара бандха.

Bandhas

Always keep the shoulder blades drawn down and apart — especially when lifting the arms overhead or entering backbends. When the blades are depressed, the arms become levers that rotate and open the chest. When the shoulders hike up, the arms cannot even rise properly.

why · mistakehide

Why Shoulder blade depression and wide setting is the structural prerequisite for the arms to function as chest-opening levers rather than neck-loading anchors.

Common mistake Hiking shoulders toward the ears during arm-raises or backbends — this immediately closes the thorax and blocks the movement.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар под Киевом. Зачем нужны базовые асаны и что такое джаландхара бандха.

Kapalabhati 4 points
+
Breath

Kapalabhati is a shat-karma (purification), not pranayama. The sharp rhythmic exhalations cause the semi-fluid brain tissue to move inside the skull — a direct physical massage of the brain. This resets habitual and obsessive neural pathway patterns, allowing you to rebuild them fresh.

why · mistakehide

Why The air jet also strikes the upper nasal cavity providing additional mechanical stimulation. It trains the diaphragm, drives venous blood from the liver and lower body back into circulation (functioning as a warmup without movement), and activates the GI tract to improve digestion.

Common mistake Treating kapalabhati as a breath-control exercise — it is a cleaning tool with specific mechanical physiological effects and should be understood in that way.

Source Что дает Капалабхати? Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Breath

Kapalabhati launches venous blood reserves stored in the liver and lower body during rest back into full active circulation — without any physical movement. This is a complete cardiovascular warmup done entirely through breathing on the mat.

why · mistakehide

Why During rest, extra blood depots in the liver and pools in lower extremities. The rhythmic diaphragmatic pumping of kapalabhati drives this blood into circulation, warming joints and tissues exactly as a jog would.

Common mistake Skipping breath practices before asana in favor of physical movement warmup only — kapalabhati achieves the full circulatory preparation effect without leaving the mat.

Source Что дает Капалабхати? Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Breath

Before starting Kapalabhati, take one full breath to open and expand the diaphragm and hold it in that open position throughout the practice. Position the head as if a crown were placed on it (slight chin retraction) so the airstream hits the upper palate and exits through the nose. The impulse for each exhale comes from the navel; the diaphragm does the mechanical work. Activation of the mula bandha area simultaneously with the navel is normal.

why · mistakehide

Why The name Kapalabhati means 'skull-shining' — the head position directs the airstream to cleanse the cranial passages. A compressed diaphragm makes the practice impossible; it must stay open as the stable container for each exhale impulse.

Common mistake Starting with a compressed diaphragm; initiating exhales from the chest; wrong head position that sends air straight out instead of hitting the upper palate.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Техника выполнения Капалабхати

Breath

Bhastrika and Kapalabhati are cleansing breaths — deliberately rapid and deep, the intentional opposite of yoga's usual goal of lengthening the breath cycle. Their purpose is cellular activation: raising the metabolic quality of the body's cells, improving the 'bricks' from which the body is built.

why · mistakehide

Why These techniques serve a different function from lengthening pranayamas: they stimulate cellular metabolism and clear stagnation rather than deepening conscious breath control.

Common mistake Applying a slow, calm approach to Bhastrika — it is specifically meant to be vigorous and rapid.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О Бхастрике

Paschimottanasana 4 points
+
Technique

Before folding forward, pull the glutes out from under the sit bones so the pelvis is not tucked. Press both legs like a gas pedal — actively. Then draw the navel to the spine and push the lower ribs forward-up while driving the sit bones back.

why · mistakehide

Why A tucked pelvis rounds the spine from the base; gas-pedal activation and navel engagement create spinal length before deepening.

Common mistake Reaching for the feet while the pelvis is tucked, rounding the spine.

Source Пашчимоттанасана. Анатолий Зенченко.

Technique

In the seated forward fold, press your feet actively against an imaginary wall in front of you, as if trying to push the wall away. Load the inner thighs. This removes tension from the posterior hamstrings and frees you to fold forward.

why · mistakehide

Why Pressing forward with the feet activates the hip flexors and creates the anterior pelvic tilt needed for a true forward fold, and transfers the work to the legs rather than straining the back.

Common mistake Pulling yourself down with the hands — this is the single most common error and activates exactly the posterior-chain protective reflex that locks the movement.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Никогда не подворачивайте копчик или держите хвост пистолетом

Technique

Before folding forward in the seated forward bend, build the base: sit vertically, scoop the sitting bones out from under the pelvis, chin toward the sternal notch, navel to spine, diaphragm in tone, and use the psoas to rotate the tail back. Only from this base can the torso move forward.

why · mistakehide

Why Without a stable vertical base the pelvis tilts backward, locking the hip flexors and forcing you to round the spine.

Common mistake Reaching forward with the hands or upper body while the base is collapsed — this folds the lumbar spine instead of rotating the pelvis.

Source Пашчимоттанасана. Асана недели. Техника выполнения от Анатолия Зенченко.

Technique

To deepen the forward fold, press your feet into an imaginary wall in front of you — activating the quadriceps. This rotates the pelvis forward and the upper body follows freely. The hands do no pulling work at all.

why · mistakehide

Why The quadriceps, through the psoas-pelvic chain, drive pelvic rotation — the true mechanism of the fold. Pulling with the hands bypasses this and loads the spine.

Common mistake Using the arms to drag the torso toward the legs, compressing the lumbar spine.

Source Пашчимоттанасана. Асана недели. Техника выполнения от Анатолия Зенченко.

Nauli 3 points
+
Bandhas

Practice Nauli to consciously de-synchronize the abdominal wall and diaphragm, which normally operate together. Progress toward independently controlling the left and right columns of spinal musculature; include short retentions after exhalation.

why · mistakehide

Why Nauli is the deepest massage of all abdominal organs; the post-exhalation retentions are unique to this practice.

Common mistake Skipping breath retentions or attempting Nauli without first mastering Uddiyana Bandha.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Как работает вакуумное втягивание - Уддияна бандха

Technique

Learn Nauli in four clear steps: (1) fully suck the abdomen in, (2) fully push it out, (3) isolate the left side, (4) isolate the right side. Only once you have clean, complete control of all four positions should you connect them into circular rotation.

why · mistakehide

Why The rotation is simply the sequential connection of these four control points; without them, you produce a shapeless belly-wave with no real neuromuscular precision.

Common mistake Attempting rotation before mastering clean left- and right-side isolation — the result looks like a random shimmy and builds nothing.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Техника пошагового освоения Наули Крийя

Anatomy

For Nauli: first establish a full uddiyana-bandha vacuum on a complete exhale. Then, while maintaining that vacuum without releasing the diaphragm, gently bring the abdominals forward into slight tone. The essential skill is de-synchronizing the diaphragm and abdominals — they normally move together, and you must learn to activate one without the other.

why · mistakehide

Why Normally diaphragm and abdominals synchronize: belly out on inhale, belly in on exhale. Nauli requires deliberately breaking this coupling — keeping the diaphragm in the high vacuum position while the rectus abdominis comes slightly forward, creating the isolated wave.

Common mistake Engaging the abdominals with too much force — this pulls the diaphragm back down, collapses the vacuum, and Nauli disappears. The abdominal tonification must be subtle.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Секреты правильного выполнения Наули

Pranayama 3 points
+
Breath

Practice pranayama seated, with a straight spine. Do not attempt to practice pranayama while in complex or contorted positions.

why · mistakehide

Why A straight spine allows the breathing apparatus to function freely and the diaphragm to move without restriction.

Common mistake Combining seated pranayama with forward folds, twists, or other shapes to 'save time.'

Source Как дышать в асанах? Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Breath

For a complete (full yoga) breath, engage both dimensions of diaphragm movement simultaneously: down and outward on the inhale, up and inward on the exhale. There is no separate lower, middle, or upper breathing — only shallow, medium, and deep.

why · mistakehide

Why Treating breathing as three separate segments fragments the diaphragm's naturally unified, three-dimensional movement.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Физиология дыхания

Breath

Classical pranayama begins at breath cycle lengths of one minute — 30 seconds of inhale, 30 seconds of exhale. The average person breathes in 3–6 second cycles. You need to increase your cycle length by a factor of 10–20 before any classical pranayama practice becomes accessible.

why · mistakehide

Why All the transformative effects described in classical texts depend on this extended cycle length; modern short-cycle 'pranayama' is an entirely different practice.

Common mistake Practicing rapid breathing exercises and calling them pranayama — this bears no resemblance to what the classical texts prescribe.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О йоге с маленькой и большой буквы

Baddha Konasana 2 points
+
Technique

First establish a vertical pelvis (like a vertical bowl). For the forward fold, internally rotate the femurs — roll the thighs inward. This is the opposite of what most schools teach. Internal rotation is what allows the pelvis to tip forward so you can lay the torso onto the feet.

why · mistakehide

Why External rotation of the femurs in this position locks the pelvis and prevents anterior tilt. Internal rotation frees the hip joint to allow the pelvis to pour forward into the fold.

Common mistake Following the widespread instruction to 'rotate the hips and knees outward' in butterfly pose — this blocks the forward fold.

Source Техника выполнения баддха конасаны - позы бабочки. Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко.

Technique

In seated hip-opening poses, rotate the pelvis and externally rotate the femurs so the thighs actually rest on the floor. Once the joint is properly aligned, the body stops tensing the ligaments to 'protect' the hip, and the legs relax naturally into the pose.

why · mistakehide

Why When the hip joint is misaligned, the body reflexively contracts ligaments and deep stabilizers to prevent structural collapse — correct alignment removes that perceived threat.

Common mistake Pressing the knees toward the floor with force before establishing correct pelvic and femoral rotation.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О правильной работе ног.

Padmasana 2 points
+
Technique

Before placing each leg in lotus, test whether you can hold the pelvis vertically with that leg already folded in. If you cannot maintain the pelvis upright, do not proceed — you are not yet ready and the knee will absorb the damage.

why · mistakehide

Why Attempting lotus with a posteriorly tilted pelvis forces the entire rotational load onto the knee's medial structures, damaging the meniscus and ligaments. The correct rotation happens at the hip, not the knee.

Common mistake Forcing the knee toward the floor or pulling the foot up with the hands without first verifying that the hip is freely externally rotating — the work is in the hip socket, not in pressing the knee down.

Source Техника входа в падмасану (позу лотоса). Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Technique

When placing one leg in lotus: bring the heel toward the navel, send the knee forward, and orient the sole toward the ceiling. The arch of the foot lodges in the crease of the hip and pelvis. The key action is external rotation of the femur in the hip socket.

why · mistakehide

Why This sequential cue ensures the thigh rotates externally in the hip joint (the correct movement for lotus), rather than the knee twisting in its hinge joint (the damaging movement).

Common mistake Lifting the foot up onto the thigh with the hands before fully externally rotating the femur — this transfers the torque to the knee, not the hip.

Source Техника входа в падмасану (позу лотоса). Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара йога.

Samakonasana 2 points
+
Technique

For the transverse split you have two options: (1) rotate each femur fully outward while keeping the pelvis in its normal orientation — this requires strong pelvic control; or (2) rotate the pelvis itself to face the floor, so the leg's natural lateral range covers the angle. In both cases the pelvis must be consciously fixed.

why · mistakehide

Why The hip joint's lateral abduction range alone is about 45 degrees. Reaching 180 degrees requires combining abduction with either external femur rotation or pelvic tilt — understanding this allows structured, progressive work.

Common mistake Pushing the legs apart without rotating either the femur or the pelvis — this jams the hip joints and makes progress impossible.

Source Работа в поперечном шпагате. Анатолий Зенченко.

Technique

To work the hip and knee joints effectively in split preparation, 'cinch' each joint: engage the thigh muscles so they grip the shin, and the shin muscles so they grip the thigh. Clearly decide whether you are fixing the thigh to get movement in the shin, or fixing the shin to get movement in the thigh.

why · mistakehide

Why A collected joint with bilateral muscular engagement is stable and generates precise, controllable movement. A loose, passive joint has no leverage and builds no neuromuscular control.

Common mistake Letting the legs flop passively into the split without muscular engagement around the hip and knee — passive collapse stretches inert structures but builds neither strength nor control.

Source Работа в поперечном шпагате. Анатолий Зенченко.

Surya Namaskar 2 points
+
Technique

In the Hindu push-up vinyasa (low plank → upward dog → downward dog), your legs should get tired, not your arms. Use leg strength to push and control the arc of the torso; arms are merely guides.

why · mistakehide

Why The legs are built to control the lever of the trunk; when the arms take over, it means the brain has simply not included the legs in the movement pattern.

Common mistake Performing the entire vinyasa with arm strength while the legs hang passively — this is why the arms exhaust and nothing strengthens in the legs.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Open Air 2015. Киев. Практика

Technique

In Surya Namaskar, maintain bandha engagement throughout the entire sequence, not just within individual postures. Match each transition to its breath: backbend on inhale, forward fold on exhale, wide lunge step on inhale. Keep bandhas actively working through every transition.

why · mistakehide

Why Bandha engagement provides structural coherence and energetic continuity through the dynamic sequence, preventing joints from losing integrity on transitions.

Common mistake Dropping the bandhas during transitions and treating them only as static holds within stable poses.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Казантип. Сурья намаскар

Uttanasana 2 points
+
Anatomy

The hamstrings (posterior thigh) are NOT what prevents a forward fold. They are acting as stabilizers because you have not engaged the muscles that actually create the fold — the iliopsoas. Engage the iliopsoas to tip the pelvis forward and the hamstrings will release automatically.

why · mistakehide

Why Every muscle has three functions: mobilization, stabilization, and terminal stabilization. If the body does not receive the mobilization signal through the correct muscles, it defaults to stabilization to prevent you from falling.

Common mistake Stretching or fighting the hamstrings; this is working on the symptom, not the cause.

Source О задней поверхности бедра. Анатолий Зенченко. · Монолог о теле. Анатолий Зенченко. · Асаны без боли. Анатолий Зенченко

Technique

In a standing forward fold, do two things simultaneously: push your lower ribs toward your knees (this lifts the head and flattens the lumbar), AND press the feet firmly into the mat by contracting the quadriceps. Do not pull the head toward the feet with your hands.

why · mistakehide

Why Pushing the lower ribs forward lengthens the lumbar spine and reduces strain in the lower back; pressing with the quads takes tension off the hamstrings from the other end.

Common mistake Pulling the head down with the hands while hanging passively in the hips — this increases hamstring strain without deepening the fold.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Open Air 2015. Киев. Практика

Adho Mukha Svanasana 1 points
+
Technique

Set up Downward Dog from a high plank — that is the correct hand-to-foot distance. Then, from mula bandha and the center of the body, push the sitting bones toward the back wall. Drive weight into the feet so the heels come down; you should be able to jump from this position.

why · mistakehide

Why The sitting bones driving back create the inverted-V from pelvic rotation, not from arm-lifting. Weight in the feet keeps the posterior chain engaged and the spine decompressed.

Common mistake Making the stance too short (the most common error) and hanging body weight through the arms.

Source Адхо Мукха Шванасана. Собака мордой вниз. Анатолий Зенченко.

Agnisara Dhauti 1 points
+
Bandhas

Agnisara Dhauti is belly-rinsing: on a retained pause after the exhale, rapidly and fully pull the belly in, then release it outward. Repeat without letting the quality of each pull-in decrease.

why · mistakehide

Why The outward push can only go as far as you pulled in — the two movements are directly proportional. This massages the abdominal organs and activates the abdominal cavity.

Common mistake The most common error: insufficient depth of pulling in (under-pulling).

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Как работает Агнисара Дхаути

Asymmetrical Asanas 1 points
+
Technique

In asymmetrical asanas — front splits, lateral bends, one-legged balances — the left side and the right side must do different things. Do not apply the same engagement cues to both sides simultaneously.

why · mistakehide

Why In an asymmetrical position, one side stabilizes while the other mobilizes. Applying identical engagement to both sides causes over-work on one side and under-work on the other, leading to strain or inefficiency.

Common mistake Treating asymmetrical poses as if they were symmetrical — applying a uniform cue to both sides — which causes one side to over-contract and blocks the very movement being sought.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Как устранить проблемы в практике

Backbends 1 points
+
Technique

In backbends, do NOT tense the glutes. Instead engage Mula Bandha, activate the legs, engage the psoas, and use the diaphragm. Keep the thighs in tone but the glutes relaxed.

why · mistakehide

Why Tensing the glutes kills Mula Bandha and worsens lumbar compression — even a small lumbar fold is amplified the moment you squeeze.

Common mistake Squeezing the glutes believing it protects the lower back.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар под Киевом. Нужно ли напрягать ягодицы делая прогиб назад

Bakasana 1 points
+
Technique

Set up crow pose with knees wider than shoulders. Weight starts in the LEGS, not the arms. Push the pelvis back and upward (as if pressing a wall behind you) with a relaxed spine — do not engage the back muscles. Transfer weight progressively into the hands while maintaining the straightest possible spine. If your legs tire in Bakasana, you are doing it correctly.

why · mistakehide

Why The hip joint fold and compression is what holds Bakasana together; the legs drive and maintain that fold. Using the back muscles to hunch into the shape is a compensation that prevents real control.

Common mistake Shifting all weight into the arms immediately and rounding the back to get the knees onto the arms; this removes the active work of the legs that stabilizes the pose.

Source Освоение бакасаны с Анатолием Зенченко.

Bhastrika 1 points
+
Breath

Bhastrika is kapalabhati intensified: both the inhalation AND the exhalation are deep and active. Give equal emphasis to both directions. The diaphragm is the primary driver — it descends on the inhale; on the exhale it rises while the lower ribs compress slightly.

why · mistakehide

Why Forced hyperventilation of the alveoli washes out residual stale air and improves alveolar gas exchange. The greater intensity also produces stronger mechanical effects on the brain and circulatory system than kapalabhati alone.

Common mistake Tilting the head back, lifting the shoulders, or breathing with the chest — and producing a hissing sound through the nose (which signals swollen nasal mucosa from irritation; remedy with neti or sutra neti practice).

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Техника выполнения Бхастрики

Halasana 1 points
+
Technique

In Halasana, after sending the legs overhead, actively push your sit-bones toward the ceiling — do not let the legs fall passively. Interlace the hands behind the back and actively draw the shoulder blades down the spine away from the ears to create a straight line through the back. This sit-bone push is driven by the upper erector spinae, diaphragm, and iliopsoas, and it engages the quadriceps.

why · mistakehide

Why Passive Halasana compresses the cervical spine; active engagement of sit-bones distributes the work along the whole back and builds a supportive straight line through the spine.

Common mistake Letting the shoulders creep toward the ears and relaxing the spine so the legs simply drape overhead — this dumps load onto the neck.

Source Халасана. Поза плуга. Анатолий Зенченко

Hip-Joint Mobility 1 points
+
Technique

Hip joint work exists in three modes: (1) fix the pelvis and move the femur; (2) fix the femur and move the pelvis; (3) move both simultaneously — the most complex. Master modes 1 and 2 before attempting mode 3.

why · mistakehide

Why Without the ability to isolate the pelvis or the femur independently, all hip-opening work is directionless — you move both simultaneously without control, creating confusion and risk of injury.

Common mistake Attempting hip mobility work without first being able to consciously hold the pelvis in a chosen position — most beginners cannot do this at all, which is the root cause of their hip 'tightness.'

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Техники «раскрытия» тазобедренных суставов

Nadi Shodhana 1 points
+
Breath

In classical Nadi Shodhana, block the nostrils with the tongue from inside — not with the fingers. Practice seated in Yoga Mudrasana (Padmasana with hands clasped behind the back), and include breath retention. The traditional prescription for purifying the subtle channels is four sessions per day of 80 breath cycles, maintained for approximately three months.

why · mistakehide

Why Nadi Shodhana is the first pranayama described in the Hatha Yoga Pradipika because without first purifying the nadis (subtle energy channels), all subsequent pranayamas lack a functioning substrate to work upon.

Common mistake A casual, simplified version without breath retention and without the classical seated position barely touches the original intention of this practice.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Нади Шодхана

Parivritta / Twists 1 points
+
Technique

In seated twists, first establish a long straight spine — push the sitting bones into the floor, then use that grounding force to lift the lower ribs upward and in the direction of the rotation. Twist from the push, not by pulling yourself around with your arms.

why · mistakehide

Why Generating the twist from ground-reaction force of the sitting bones creates an active, structurally supported rotation. Using the arm as a lever to haul the torso around produces a limp, passive rotation without structural support.

Common mistake Using the arm as a fulcrum to drag the torso into rotation while the trunk hangs limp — the twist will be shallow and there is no structural integration.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О том, как правильно скручиваться.

Prasarita Padottanasana 1 points
+
Technique

Free the pelvis first: rotate and release the sit bones outward and back. Once the pelvis is free, the spine can lengthen and follow. The spine follows the pelvis — always liberate the pelvis before working the spine.

why · mistakehide

Why The spine attaches to the pelvis; if the pelvis is locked, the spine cannot extend regardless of effort.

Common mistake Pulling the torso down while the pelvis is locked, creating rounding.

Source Секреты освоения Прасарита Падоттанасаны. Анатолий Зенченко.

Sarvangasana 1 points
+
Technique

Enter Sarvangasana from Halasana: draw the shoulders away from the ears, slide the shoulder blades down the back toward the pelvis, and stabilize the thorax, lumbar, and pelvis. Press the hands into the back as close to the shoulder blades as possible; narrow the elbows to approximately shoulder width. Lift hips and legs straight up into one vertical line — do not let the hips drift backward. Pull the navel to the spine, engage Mula Bandha, push the feet toward the ceiling. Quadriceps should be active; glutes should be relaxed.

why · mistakehide

Why The foundation of the pose is the shoulder-blade-to-spine connection created in Halasana, not brute shoulder or neck strength. Entering from Halasana ensures the shoulder girdle is properly stabilized before the inversion load is applied.

Common mistake Splaying the elbows wide transfers the load to the outer edges of the shoulders and destabilizes the pose. Letting the hips drift backward creates a bent, compressed spinal column instead of a clean vertical inversion.

Source Сарвангасана. Анатолий Зенченко. Ишвара Йога.

Shatkarma 1 points
+
Method

The six purification practices are not merely physical cleansing. Their deeper purpose is learning to bring smooth (involuntary) muscle under conscious control — which Western medicine considers impossible. You are learning to befriend and influence the subconscious.

why · mistakehide

Why Smooth muscle governs digestion, circulation, and organ function; voluntary influence over it expands what you can consciously regulate.

Common mistake Treating Shatkarma purely as hygiene.

Source Анатолий Зенченко. Основные техники йоги

Shavasana 1 points
+
Method

Shavasana in hatha yoga is simply a physical relaxation posture — appropriate briefly after a tiring practice. Lying in it for 40 minutes wastes class time. If you practiced correctly, working from the inside, you may arrive at the end of class in such a balanced, harmonious state that you do not need it at all.

why · mistakehide

Why Using long shavasana as a ritual filler reduces the actual asana work. Deep physical recovery after genuine effort is valuable; padding class time with lying down is not.

Common mistake Taking 5-minute shavasanas between every asana — this turns the practice into 2-3 postures surrounded by prolonged lying down.

Source Ишвара-йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О шавасане и йоге-нидре.

Surya Bhedana 1 points
+
Breath

Use Surya Bhedana when you need to increase energy, warm the body, and remove sluggishness or excess mucus — it activates the fire quality in the body. Balance it when necessary with cooling pranayamas such as Sheetali and Sheetkari, which have the opposite effect.

why · mistakehide

Why Pranayamas have opposing energetic qualities: solar practices (right nostril breathing) increase metabolic fire; lunar practices cool and calm. Knowing which to apply according to your current state is an essential practical skill.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О пользе Сурьи Бхедана

Tadasana 1 points
+
Technique

Set correct spinal alignment by doing two things simultaneously: push the sternum and lower ribs forward and upward; send the sitting bones backward. Reinforce this ideal natural position at the start of practice and maintain it throughout all asanas.

why · mistakehide

Why This action sets the lumbar and thoracic curves to their natural state without contracting the back muscles, creating the axial support base for all other work. The open diaphragm and retracted navel reinforce and maintain this alignment.

Common mistake Tucking the tailbone under (posterior pelvic tilt) or holding the tail 'like a gun' (excessive anterior tilt) — both destroy the natural lumbar curve and cause spinal compression.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Никогда не подворачивайте копчик или держите хвост пистолетом · Анатолий Зенченко. Семинар под Киевом

Trikonasana 1 points
+
Technique

In revolved triangle with the left foot forward, the twist is generated by the back (right) side: right psoas pushes the back wall, right side of the diaphragm anchors down, right arm pushes the floor. The front side simply releases. The top arm lifts as a result, not as a cause.

why · mistakehide

Why Using the back-body as the active driver grounds the pose and prevents a shoulder-torquing collapse. The asymmetric psoas-diaphragm action creates safe rotation.

Common mistake Forcing the twist by pulling with the upper arm, which destabilizes the pelvis and strains the lower back.

Source Паривритта Триконасана. Анатолий Зенченко.

Ujjayi 1 points
+
Breath

In Ujjayi, narrow the glottis on both inhalation and exhalation. This resistance forces your breathing muscles to work significantly harder, intensifies gas exchange in the lungs, and keeps the alveoli inflated and open rather than sticking together.

why · mistakehide

Why The added resistance during both phases of breathing creates negative and positive pressure fluctuations that mechanically expand the alveoli and train the respiratory musculature more effectively than unresisted breathing.

Common mistake Breathing superficially or only constricting the glottis on one phase; treating Ujjayi as a sound technique rather than a resistance training technique for breathing muscles.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. Зависимость газообмена в легких от наличия жиров

Urdhva Mukha Svanasana 1 points
+
Technique

In backbends, use the diaphragm to lift and open the thoracic spine — do not collapse into the lumbar. Without diaphragm involvement you will get a painful block in the lower back.

why · mistakehide

Why The diaphragm is what allows the thoracic cage to open and rise; without it, all backbend load concentrates in the lumbar joints.

Common mistake Tucking the tailbone to 'protect' the lower back — this simply removes the backbend entirely and forces the body to compensate by loading the knees and neck instead.

Source О роли диафрагмы. Анатолий Зенченко. Методика Ишвара йога.

Viloma 1 points
+
Breath

Take a smooth, calm, long inhalation, then a brief pause. Then exhale in steps: exhale 2 seconds, pause 2 seconds, exhale 2 seconds, pause 2 seconds — continuing step by step until the breath is complete. The more steps you can create on one exhalation, the better.

why · mistakehide

Why Stepped exhalation develops fine control of the expiratory muscles and extends exhalation capacity, which deepens the parasympathetic response and trains breath retention.

Common mistake Rushing through the steps; making the initial inhalation too short; taking more than a brief pause before starting the exhalation phase.

Source Ишвара йога. Анатолий Зенченко. О Вилома-пранаяме

Virasana 1 points
+
Method

Every joint in every asana must be 'gathered' — assembled and ready to both absorb shock and propel. Even sitting in Virasana, ask: can I jump from here? If the knee joints are not gathered, you cannot. Gather them and you can.

why · mistakehide

Why A gathered joint is actively stabilized by balanced muscular tension. A limp or over-extended joint is neither a good shock absorber nor capable of generating force.

Common mistake Passively settling into joint positions in seated or standing poses without actively gathering them.

Source Критерий собранности суставов или как подпрыгнуть в Вирасане. Анатолий Зенченко.

Method · captions + Whisper large-v3 → 219 teachings, aggregated by theme and asana.
Note · a study reading of your teacher's direction — not medical advice. When in doubt, ask Anatoly on the mat.
